title: முதல் சருக்கம் 0-19 (1/2)
theme: The poet invokes the tirthankaras and Vani, apologises for his flawed verse and says his tale comes from the Jain Anga texts; he then places the story in Magadha under King Shrenika, who goes with army and queen to the hill where the lord has come and ends with a hymn praising the lord for conquering karma.
source_issues: Verse 0 is the invocation before verse 1 and is kept as number 0; the traditional count is 170.
Verse 9, line 3: 'சாலி னீதா' appears to carry the queen's name Chalini in broken word division.
Verses 16 to 19 print eight half-lines each; joined into four lines.

cast.role: King of Magadha at Rajamagiri, who goes to worship the tirthankara and praises him
the forest-keeper who reports the wonders of the hill to the king
the tirthankara who comes to the hill Vipula; praised as Sri Vardhamanan
the king's chief queen
the lord Nemi, to whose feet the poet bows in the invocation

tamil: அணிமலர்ப் பிண்டி யின்கீ ழமர்ந்த நேமீசர் பாதம்
பணியவே வாணி பாதம் பண்ணவர் தமக்கு மெந்தம்
இணைகரஞ் சிரசிற் கூப்பி யியல்புறத் தொழுது மன்றே.
reading: The poet opens by joining his hands over his head and worshipping the feet of Lord Nemi, seated under the flowering pindi tree beneath the three umbrellas, and the feet of Vani.
nuance: The invocation is not part of the traditional count of 170 and is kept as verse 0. It names Nemi, while the hymn at verses 16-19 praises Sri Vardhamanan; the poem addresses two tirthankaras. Vani is the goddess of speech, named after the lord.
event: The poet raises his joined hands and worships the lord's feet.

tamil: செந்தளிர்ப் பிண்டி யின்கீழ்ச் செழுமணி மண்ட பத்துள்
இந்திர னினிதி னேத்து மேந்தரி யாச னத்தின்
அந்தமா யமர்ந்த கோவி னருள்புரி தீர்த்த காலங்
கொந்தல ராசன் நாக குமரனற் கதைவி ரிப்பாம்.
reading: The poet says he will spread out the tale of the Naga prince, the king who wears blossoms, in the age of the tirtha-lord who sat under the pindi tree.
nuance: The tale is dated by the presence of a tirthankara, which sets the whole story inside the Jain teaching age.

tamil: திங்கள் முந்நான்கு யோகந் தீவினை யரிய நிற்பர்
அங்கபூ வாதி நூலு ளரிப்பறத் தெளிந்த நெஞ்சிற்
தங்கிய கருணை யார்ந்த தவமுனி யவர்கள் சொன்ன
பொங்குநற் கவிக்க டறான் புகுந்துநீர்த் தெழுந்த தன்றே.
reading: The poet says his poem rose from the words of compassionate ascetics who keep twelve-month yoga and have clearly learned the Anga and Purva texts.
nuance: The poem takes its authority from named Jain scripture and from ascetics' speech, not from its own invention.

tamil: இகழ்ச்சியி னீப்பா ரில்லை யீண்டுநற் பொருளு ணர்ந்தோர்
அகத்தினி மதியிற் கொள்வா ரரியரோ வெனது சொல்லைச்
செகத்தவ ருணர்ந்து கேட்கச் செப்புதற் பால தாமே.
reading: The poet argues that people do not discard a bright lamp because of its smoke, so those who grasp the worth of a thing will keep his words in mind.
nuance: The lamp-and-soot image is the apology convention of the epics; here the flaw is conceded, not denied.

tamil: வெவ்வினை வெகுண்டு வாரா விக்கிநன் கடைக்கும் வாயகள்
செவ்விதிற் புணர்ந்து மிக்க செல்வத்தை யாக்கு முன்னங்
கவ்விய கரும மெல்லாங் கணத்தினி லுதிர்ப்பை யாக்கும்
இவ்வகைத் தெரிவு றுப்பார்க் கினிதுவைத் துரைத்து மன்றே.
reading: The poet says that deeds seized earlier can be shed in an instant, and that he tells this sweetly to those who discern it.
nuance: This verse, unlike the Naladiyar's, says old deeds can be dropped rather than only borne; the first two lines are hard to parse.

tamil: நாவலந் தீப நூற்றை நண் ணுதொண் ணூறு கூறில்
ஆவதன் னொருகூ றாகு மரியநற் பரத கண்டம்
பாவலர் தகைமை மிக்கோர் பரம்பிய தரும பூமி
reading: Bharata land, the Dharma-earth, is a ninetieth part of Jambudvipa, and in it lies the country of Magadha with cloud-wrapped groves.
nuance: Dharma-land (தரும பூமி) is the Jain geography: only here can karma be earned and ended.

tamil: திசைகளெங் கெங்குஞ் செய்யாள் செறிந்தினி துறையு நாட்டுள்
இசையுநற் பாரி சாத வினமலர்க் காவுஞ் சூழ்ந்த
அசைவிலா வமர லோகத் ததுநிக ரான மண்ணுள்
இசையுலா நகர மிக்க விராசமா கிரிய மாமே.
reading: In Magadha, where Lakshmi dwells in all directions, stands the city Rajamagiri, rivalling the heavens with its flower groves.

tamil: கிடங்கரு கிஞ்சி யோங்கிக் கிளர்முகில் சூடிச் செம்பொன்
கடங்கள்வைத் திலங்கு மாடங் கதிர்மதி சூட்டி னாற்போல்
படங்கிடந் தல்கு லார்கள் பாடலோ டாட லாலே
இடங்கொண்ட வின்ப மும்ப ரிடத்தையு மெச்சு மன்றே.
reading: The city's towers, raised above its moat, crowned with moon and cloud, are full of singing and dancing women whose joy rivals that of the gods.

tamil: பாரித்த தன்மை முன்னம் பாலித்தற் கைம்ம டங்காம்
பூரித்த தார்கள் வேய்ந்த பொற்குடை யெழுந்த மேகம்
வாரித்த திசைந்த ளிக்கும் வண்கையம் பொற்றிண் டோளான்
reading: The ruler of this land is Shrenika, of the golden umbrella and the generous hand, guarding all who are his.

tamil: ஆறிலொன் றிறைகொண் டாளு மரசன்மா தேவி யன்னப்
பேறுடை நடைவேற் கண்ணாள் பெறற்கருங் கற்பி னாள்போ
வீறுடைச் சாலி னீதா மிடைதவழ் கொங்கை கொண்டை
நாறுடைத் தார ணிந்த நகைமதி முகத்தி னாளே.
reading: Chalini, his chief queen, is described as a woman of steady chastity whose face is like the moon.
nuance: The virtue named is the ordinary wifely karpu, praised as rare (பெறற்கரும்).

tamil: மற்றுமெண் ணாயி ரம்பேர் மன்னனுக் கினிய மாதர்
வெற்றிவேல் விழியி னாரும் வேந்தனு மினிய போகம்
உற்றுடன் புணர்ந்து வின்பத் துவகையு ளழுந்தி யங்குச்
செற்றவர்ச் செகுத்துச் செங்கோற் செலவிய காலத் தன்றே
reading: Besides the queen, eight thousand beloved wives share his pleasures, and he destroys his foes and rules by the straight sceptre.
nuance: Pleasure and just rule are given together as the king's glory, as the epic's first picture of a good king.
event: The king enjoys his women and destroys his enemies while ruling.

tamil: இஞ்சிசூழ் புரத்து மேற்பா லிலங்கிய விபுல மென்னும்
மஞ்சிசூழ் மலையின் மீது வரவீர நாதர் வந்து
இஞ்சிமூன் றிலங்கும் பூமி யேழிறை யிருக்கை வட்டம்
அஞ்சிலம் பார்க ளாட வமரருஞ் சூழ்ந்த வன்றே.
reading: On the hill Vipula, west of the walled city, Lord Vira comes, and gods and heavenly women gather round the assembly hall of three walls and seven levels.
nuance: The hall of three walls is the samavasarana, the Jain preaching-hall of a tirthankara.
event: The lord Vira arrives on Vipula hill and the gods assemble.

tamil: நனைமது மலர்க ளேந்தி நன்னகர் புகுந்தி ராசன்
மனையது மதிற்க டந்து மன்னனை வணங்கிச் செப்ப
மனமிக மகிழ்ந்தி றைஞ்சி மாமுர சறைக வென்றான்.
reading: The forest-keeper sees the wonders of the wood, brings flowers to the king, bows, and reports; the king rejoices and has the great drum beaten.
event: The forest-keeper reports the wonders to the king, who has the drum sounded.

tamil: இடிமுர சார்ப்பக் கேட்டு மியம்பிய வத்தி னத்தின்
படுமத யானை தேர்மா வாள்நாற் படையுஞ் சூழக்
கடிமலர் சாந்து மேந்திக் காவலன் றேவி யோடுங்
கொடிநிரை பொன்னே யிற்குக் குழுவுடன் சென்ற வன்றே.
reading: At the thunder of the drum the army of elephants, chariots, horses and swords gathers, and the king sets out with his queen to the golden walls.
event: The king sets out with his army and queen to the golden walls.

tamil: பொன்னெயிற் குறுகிக் கைம்மாப் புரவல னிழிந்துட் புக்கு
நன்னிலத் ததிச யங்கள் நரபதி தேவி யர்க்குப்
பன்னுரை செய்து காட்டிப் பரமன்றன் கோயி றன்னை
இன்னியல் வலங்கொண் டெய்தி யீசனை யிறைஞ்சி னானே.
reading: The king enters the golden wall, shows the queens the wonders there, circles the lord's hall and bows.
event: The king enters, shows the queens the wonders, circles the hall and worships the lord.

tamil: நிலமுறப் பணிந்தெ ழுந்து நிகரிலஞ் சினையின் முற்றிக்
கலனணி செம்பொன் மார்பன் கால்பொரு கடலிற் பொங்கி
நலமுறு தோத்தி ரங்கள் நாதன்றன் வதன நோக்கிப்
பலமன மின்றி யொன்றிப் பலதுதி செப்ப லுற்றான்.
reading: The king falls to the earth, rises, and, welling up like the sea, begins many hymns, gazing on the lord's face with one mind.
event: The king bows, rises and begins to praise the lord.

tamil: பொறியொடுவல் வினைவென்ற புனித னீயே பூநான்கு மலர்ப்பிண்டிப் போத னீயே
புறவிதழ்சேர் மரைமலர்மேல் விரனால் விட்டுப் பொன்னெயிலுண் மன்னியபுங் கவனு நீயே
அறவிபணி பணவரங்கத் தமர்ந்தாய் நீயே ஐங்கணைவில் மன்மதனை யகன்றாய் நீயே
செறிபுகழ்சேர் சித்திநகர் தன்னை யாளும் சிரீவர்த்த மானனெனுந் தீர்த்த னீயே.
reading: The king praises the lord as the one who conquered hard deeds with the senses, who sits under the pindi tree, who left Kama, and who now rules the city of release as Sri Vardhamanan.
nuance: The first of four hymn verses ending with the refrain on Sri Vardhamanan; the printed eight half-lines were joined into four.
event: The king hymns the lord's victory over karma and his seat under the pindi tree.

tamil: கஞ்சமலர் திருமார்பிற் றரித்தாய் நீயே காலமொரு மூன்றுணர்ந்த கடவு ணீயே
பஞ்சாத்தி தானுரைத்த பரம னீயே பரமநிலை யொன்றெனவே பணித்தாய் நீயே
துஞ்சாநல் லுலகுதொழுந் தூய னீயே தொல்வினையெல் லாமெரித்த துறவ னீயே
செஞ்சொற் பாவையை நாவிற் சேர்த்தாய் நீயே சிரீவர்த்த மானெனுந் தீர்த்த னீயே.
reading: The king praises the lord for all-knowing in three times, for burning all old deeds, for teaching the five categories, and for placing the tongue under speech.
nuance: Karma here is burned by the lord's own renunciation; in the Saiva books it is burned by grace.
event: The king continues the hymn.

tamil: அறவனீ யமலனீ யாதி நீயே ஆரியனீ சீரீயனீ யனந்த னீயே
திரிலோக லோகமொடு தேய னீயே தேவாதி தேவனெனுந் தீர்த்த னீயே
எரிமணிநற் பிறப்புடைய யீச னீயே இருநான்கு குணமுடைய யிறைவ னீயே
திரிபுவனந் தொழுதிறைஞ்சுஞ் செல்வ னீயே சிரீவர்த்த மானமெனுந் தீர்த்த னீயே.
reading: The king calls him righteous, spotless, ageless, endless, god of gods, the lord of eight qualities, worshipped by the three worlds.
nuance: The eight qualities are named only as a number here; the verse does not list them.
event: The king continues the hymn.

tamil: முனிவர்தமக் கிறையான மூர்த்தி நீயே மூவா முதல்வனெனு முத்த னீயே
இனிமையா னந்தசுகத் திருந்தாய் நீயே இயலாறு பொருளுரைத்த வீச னீயே
முனிவுமுத லில்லாத முனைவ னீயே முக்குடையின் கீழமர்ந்த முதல்வ னீயே
செனித்திறக்கு மூப்பி றப்புந் தீர்த்தாய் நீயே சிரீவர்த்த மானனெனுந் தீர்த்த னீயே.
reading: The king ends the hymn praising the lord as free of anger and of birth, old age and death, who taught the six substances and sits under the three umbrellas.
event: The king ends his hymn to the lord.

title: முதல் சருக்கம் 20-39 (2/2)
theme: The king of Magadha, having praised the lord and bowed to Gautama, asks for the Sri Panchami tale; Gautama begins it in Kanakapura, where King Jayandhara falls for a painted woman and marries Prithidevi, who fears the senior queen's envy, takes refuge in the lord of non-killing and is promised a virtuous son.
source_issues: Verse 20 is printed in eight half-lines and the build joined them into four lines.
Verse 27's last two lines run together four names (மதுத்தாரணி, சீதரன், நயந்தரன்) so the roles cannot be fixed.
Verses 21, 29 and 34 contain words with stray spacing or typos (பாவலன் புக்கதே; கின்னரி யோகிளர்; வாரணி கொங்கை) and the sense there is read, not certain.

cast.role: the king of the frame who hears the Sri Panchami tale from Gautama
the queen who listens with him
the lord the king praises in verse 20
the chief disciple (ganadhara) who tells the tale
king of Kanakapura in Magadha, in the tale
Jayandhara's senior queen
the king's other consorts, as a group
the merchant who shows the portrait and describes Prithidevi
daughter of Srivarman of Parangiri, Jayandhara's new chief queen
Prithidevi's nurse, who answers the woman at the elephant
the sage Prithidevi worships at the temple

tamil: நவபதநன் னயமாறு நவின்றாய் நீயே நன்முனிவர் மனத்திசைந்த னாத னீயே
உவமையிலா வைம்பதமு முரைத்தாய் நீயே உத்தமர்த மிருதயத்து ளுகந்தாய் நீயே
பவமயமா மிருவினையைப் பகர்ந்தாய் நீயே பரம நிலையமர்ந்த பரமன் நீயே
சிவமயமாய் நின்றதிகழ் தேச னீயே சிரீவர்த்த மானனெனுந் தீர்த்த னீயே.
reading: The speaker addresses the lord again and again as 'you': you set out the good way of the nine categories, you spoke the five unequalled ranks, you declared the two deeds that make up becoming, you are the radiant one standing as bliss and the pure ford called Vardhamana.
nuance: The verse was printed in eight half-lines and the edition's join into four is the text used. சிவமயமாய் here describes the lord as made of auspiciousness or release, not the Saiva god. The speaker is not named in the verse; the next verse says the king did 'praises' and then went on, so the king is the likely voice.

reading: After his praises the king, whose long arms are like two treasures, bows with a settled mind toward the pure jewelled ground and goes into the holy place of the lord of ascetics.
nuance: Line 4 reads பாவலன் புக்கதே; the sense of பாவலன் (poet, or an epithet of the king) and the object of the entry are not fixed by the verse.
event: The king, after praising the lord, bows and enters the place where the lord's teacher sits.

reading: The teacher of the assembly takes in the lord's good word and, seated, pours the rain of dharma on living beings; the king bows at the pure feet of that renunciant.
nuance: The teaching is handed on in two steps, lord to ganadhara to hearers, and the verse makes the teacher the one who rains it; the verse does not name him, and 23 names Gautama.
event: The ganadhara expounds the lord's word to living beings and the king bows to his feet.

reading: The king, having reached the flower-like feet of the great sage, bows at the victorious feet of Gautama, chief of good ascetics.
event: The king bows at Gautama's feet.

reading: The king and his queen, who bow with both hands, listen with joy to Gautama's teaching of the nature of dharma, and when they have heard it,
nuance: The verse is an unfinished sentence and the next verse supplies its main clause; the claim is thin because the content of the teaching is not given here.
event: The king and queen hear Gautama teach the true nature of dharma.

reading: The king asks that the story of Sri Panchami be told, and the teacher, who dwells in knowledge, vision and conduct, takes his sign and begins to speak.
nuance: அறிவு காட்சி ஒழுக்கம் are the three jewels of the Jain path as the verse names them together; the verse does not call them that. The frame sets up everything after it as Gautama's telling of an earlier birth story.
event: The king asks Gautama to tell the Sri Panchami story and Gautama begins.

reading: In the Bharata land of the island of Jambu lies Magadha with its fine cities; Kanakapura, ringed with koel-filled groves, is in it.
The lord of that city is Jayandhara, whose good wife is Visalanetrai; the verse goes on to name a son, Sridhara, and Nayandhara, with the sense of 'good minister' attached to one of them.
nuance: The last two lines run names together (மதுத்தாரணி, சீதரன், நயந்தரன்), so which name belongs to the son and which to the minister cannot be fixed from the Tamil; I read சுதன் as 'son' and நன்கமைச்சன் as the minister.

reading: While the king enjoys his eight thousand queens, a merchant shows him the form of a woman painted on a gold vessel among his many wares.
nuance: The king is unmoved by thousands of wives until a picture arrives; the story starts from a want that none of the existing queens meet.
event: A merchant shows King Jayandhara a portrait of a woman on a gold vessel.

reading: The king, struck and delighted by the picture, asks whether such a form is of a kinnari, a yogini or a dark woman, and Vasavan the merchant begins to answer.
event: The king, bewildered by the picture, asks who she is, and the merchant Vasavan replies.

reading: The merchant says: in the land of Surashtra, in the populous Parangiri, lives Srivarman, whose wife Srimati bears a daughter named Prithidevi.
nuance: The speaker is read from the previous verse; the verse itself does not name him.

reading: The merchant tells of her rightly; the king calls her and, in a rite before the sacred fire, unites with her.
nuance: தெய்வ வேள்வி is a rite of the sacred fire, and the verse does not say whether it is a wedding in a Jain form; the epic's affiliation is by tradition only.
event: Jayandhara has Prithidevi brought and marries her before the sacred fire.

reading: The king, pleased, gives her the rank of chief queen, and when the other wives come to bow to her, they go on in this way.
nuance: The verse ends on 'ones who go on together', a clause the next verse finishes.
event: Jayandhara makes Prithidevi chief queen and the other consorts come to honour her.

reading: For the spring game the king and his women go happily to a flower garden, and Prithidevi leaves in a palanquin to watch the water-sport of an elephant.
event: The court goes to the garden and Prithidevi rides out to see the elephant's bathing.

reading: A woman standing in the road before the elephant asks who the lady with the belted breasts is, and the nurse answers that she is the king's chief queen.
nuance: That the woman at the elephant is Visalanetrai is read from the next verse, not stated here; who asks and to whom the nurse speaks is not fixed by the Tamil.
event: A woman before the elephant asks about Prithidevi and the nurse says she is the king's chief queen.

tamil: வேல்விழி மாது கேட்டு விசாலநேத் திரையோ வென்னைக்
கான்மிசை வீழ வெண்ணிக் காண்டற்கு நின்றா ளென்று
பான்மொழி யமிர்த மன்னாள் பரம னாலைய மடைந்து
நூன்மொழி யிறைவன் பாதம் நோக்கிநன் கிறைஞ்சி னாளே.
reading: The spear-eyed woman hears this and thinks that Visalanetrai stands there to see her fall at the elephant's foot, then goes to the temple and bows to the feet of the lord whose word is scripture.
nuance: The fear is the new queen's own supposition and the verse never shows Visalanetrai doing or wishing anything; only the suspicion of rivalry and the turn to the god are given. The reading 'to fall at its feet' (கான்மிசை வீழ) is mine and the elephant is not named in the verse.
event: Prithidevi, fearing the senior queen means her harm, goes to the temple and bows to the lord.

reading: Praising the lord who keeps the vow of not killing, she says that those who bow to him cut off the evil birth and reach release easily, and she bids the sage who binds all deeds to teach her.
nuance: The god is defined by a vow, not a gift: what he gives is the example; the verse does not say whether the worship or the vow does the cutting. இயன்முனி in line 4 may be a different person from the lord, and the verse does not say.
event: Prithidevi praises the lord of non-killing and asks the sage to teach her.

reading: As she bows, the sage blesses her and she asks whether good penance can be hers; he tells her that she will get a son of countless virtues, with fame.
nuance: She asks about tapas and he answers with a son, so the answer is to a different question or the question means 'will my wish for a worthy end be met'; the sense of நற்றவம் ஆமோ is open.
event: The sage blesses Prithidevi and foretells a famous, virtuous son.

reading: She goes on with her people, takes up the penance and hears the teaching of dharma with joy, bows without stain at the feet of the lord who conquered fate, and is glad as if a son were already born.
nuance: விதி here is the deed-fate the lord has won over, not an outside power; the verse says tavam is entered but does not say what vow, and 'took penance' may only mean she kept a lay observance.
event: Prithidevi takes penance, hears dharma and bows to the lord, delighted as if her son were born.

tamil: நற்றவ னுரைத்த சொல்லை நறுமலர்க் கோதை கேட்டு
பற்றுட னுணர்ந்து நல்ல பாசிழைப் பரவை யல்குல்
உற்றதன் குழலி னாரோ டுறுதவன் பாதந் தன்னில்
வெற்றியி னிறைஞ்சி வந்து வியன்மனை புகுந்தி ருந்தாள்
reading: Hearing the good ascetic's words, the garlanded woman understands them with attachment and, with her women, bows in triumph at his feet, returns to her great house and sits.
event: Prithidevi hears the sage, bows with her women and goes home.

title: இரண்டாம் சருக்கம் 40-56 (1/2)
theme: The queen's temple visit and her dream of a bull and a young sun are read by a sage as the coming of a son who will rule, take up austerity and end his karma; the boy is born, the temple doors open at his foot and a serpent holds him safe in the pond, so he is named Naga Kumaran, and the chapter closes on a courtesan's daughters offered to him.
source_issues: 49 line 2 was printed with a stray pulli (FLAG repaired); the repair reads correctly.
46 lines 3-4, 48 lines 3-4 and 53 line 3 are obscure or damaged; readings of them are marked uncertain.
55 lines 3-4 give the exchange between king and prince with no marks of speech.

cast.role: the king of the city, Naga Kumara's father
the chief queen, the prince's mother
the sage at the Jina temple who reads the dream
the naked sage who gives the signs
the prince, born in this chapter
the mother of the courtesan girls
the courtesan girls Kinnari and Manokari

tamil: வனவிளை யாட லாடி மன்னன் றன்மனை புகுந்து
மனமகிழ் கோதை தன்னை மருவிய காத லாலே
புனலினீ யாட லின்றிப் போம்பொருட் புகல்க வென்ன
கனவரை மார்பன் கேட்பக் காரிகை யுரைக்கு மன்றே.
reading: Back from sporting in the forest, the king enters his house and the queen, loving, is asked to say what matter is lost for want of water-play; she will speak while he listens.
nuance: Lines 3-4 are hard to construe: who asks and what 'the matter that goes' (போம்பொருள்) is are not fixed, and the verse only says the queen will speak.
event: The king returns from forest play to the queen's house, and the queen is about to tell him something.

tamil: இறைவனா லயத்துட் சென்று விறைவனை வணங்கித் தீய
கறையிலா முனிவன் பாதங் கண்டடி பணிந்து தூய
அறவுரை கேட்டே னென்ன வரசன்கேட் டுளம கிழ்ந்து
பிறைநுதற் பேதை தன்னாற் பெறுசுவைக் கடலு ளாழ்ந்தார்.
reading: The queen says she went to the god's temple, bowed to the Jina and to the stainless sage, heard pure teaching of virtue, and the king, glad at hearing it, sinks with her into a sea of delight.
nuance: The teaching is called அறவுரை but its content is not given; the verse joins temple worship and household pleasure in one scene.
event: The queen reports her visit to the temple and the sage's sermon; the king rejoices.

tamil: இருவரும் பிரித லின்றி யின்புறு போகந் துய்த்து
மருவிய துயில்கொள் கின்றார் மனோகர மென்னும் யாமம்
இருண்மனை இமிலே றொன்று மிளங்கதிர் கனவிற் றோன்றப்
பொருவிலாட் கண்டெ ழுந்து புரவலர்க் குணர்த்தி னாளே.
reading: After shared pleasure the couple sleep, and in the night's watch the queen sees in a dream a bull and a young sun and wakes the king to tell him.
nuance: The verse names the omens but not what they mean; the answer waits in verse 44.
event: The queen dreams of a bull and a young sun and wakes the king to tell him.

tamil: வேந்தன்கேட் டினிய னாகி விமலனா லயத்துட் சென்று
சேந்தளிர்ப் பிண்டி யின்கீழ்ச் செல்வனை வணங்கி வாழ்த்தி
காந்திய முனிக்கி றைஞ்சிக் கனாப்பய னுவல வென்றான்
ஏந்திள முலையி னாளு மிறைவனு மிகுந்து கேட்டார்.
reading: The pleased king goes to the temple, bows to the Lord under the red-leaved pindi tree and the sage, and asks for the fruit of the dream, which the queen and he hear with joy.
event: The king takes the dream to the sage at the temple and asks its meaning.

tamil: அம்முனி யவரை நோக்கி யருந்துநற் கனவு தன்னைச்
செம்மையி னிருவர் கட்குஞ் சிறுவன்வந் துதிக்கு மென்றுங்
கம்பமின் னிலங்க ளெல்லாங் காத்துநற் றவமுந் தாங்கி
வெம்பிய வினைய றுத்து வீடுநன் கடையு மென்றார்.
reading: The sage tells them that the dream means a son will be born to both, who will guard the whole earth, bear great austerity, cut away his heated deeds and reach release.
nuance: The sage gives the son two lives, the protector of lands and the ascetic who ends karma; the prophecy sets both before the story of the prince's marriages and later renunciation begins. The word வினை here is the deeds that burn away through his own tapas, not a grace from another.
event: The sage reads the dream: a son will be born who will rule, take up austerity and end his karma in release.

tamil: தனையன்வந் துதித்த பின்னைத் தகுகுறிப் புண்டோ வென்று
புனைமல ரலங்கல் மார்பன் புரவலன் மற்றுங் கேட்ப
நினைமினக் குறிக ளுண்டென் னேர்மையிற் கேட்பி ராயின்
தினையனைப் பற்று மில்லாத் திகம்பர னியம்பு கின்றான்.
reading: The king asks whether there are signs after the son is born, and a naked sage, free of the smallest attachment, says that he will tell them if they listen with honesty.
nuance: திகம்பரன் (sky-clad) is the sage's own title, so the speaker here may be a different monk from the one in 44; the verse does not say.
event: The king asks for signs of the son's coming; a Digambara sage agrees to name them.

reading: The sage gives the signs: the doors of the golden-walled Jina's temple will open at the touch of the son's foot, he will rise from the pond of nagas, and with the king of nagas he will curb pride.
nuance: Lines 3-4 are obscure (நன்னாக வாவிதனில் அழுவப் பதமுண்டாம், மன்னாக மாவினொடு மதமடக்கி): whether the nagas are the pond's serpents or a naga king, and whose pride is curbed, is not fixed.
event: The sage lists signs by which the son will be known.

reading: The king and queen bow and praise the sage, return to their fine house and live happily on the bed in the upper hall.
event: The royal couple leave the temple and return to their palace.

tamil: புண்டவழ் வேற்கண் கோதை பூரண மயற்கைச் சின்னம்
மண்ணினி துண்ண வெண்ணு மைந்தன்பூ வலய மாளும்
பண்ணுகக் கிளவி வாயிற் பரவிய தீருஞ் சேரும்
கண்ணிய மிச்ச மின்னைக் கழித்திடு முறுப்பி தாமே.
reading: The queen, in the first mark of pregnancy, longs to eat earth, and the verse says the son will rule the world, with some words of the rest too damaged to read.
nuance: The verse is badly corrupt after line 2; only the craving for earth (மண்ணினிது உண்ண) and the son who will rule the world are clear.
event: The queen shows the craving of pregnancy and the child's rule is foretold.

tamil: திங்க ளொன்பான் நிறைந்து செல்வனற் றினத்திற் றோன்றப்
பொங்குநீர்க் கடல்போல் மன்னன் புரிந்துநல் லுவகை யாகித்
தங்குபொன் னறைதி றந்து தரணியுள் ளவர்க்குச் சிந்திச்
சிங்கநேர் சிறுவ னாமம் சீர்பிரதா பந்த னென்றார்.
reading: In the ninth month the son is born on a good day, the king opens his golden store and scatters wealth over the land, and the boy is named Pirathapan.
nuance: The child is named Pirathapan (சீர்பிரதாபந்தன்) here, and only after the pond is he called Naga Kumaran in 53.
event: The son is born, the king gives out gold and names him Pirathapan.

tamil: பிரிதிவிழ் தேவி யோர்நாள் பெருங்குழுத் தேவி மாரும்
அரியநற் பரமன் கோயி லன்புடன் போக வெண்ணி
விரிநிற மலருஞ் சாந்தும் வேண்டிய பலவு மேந்திப்
பரிவுள தனையற் கொண்டு பாங்கினாற் சென்ற வன்றே.
reading: One day the queen and the chief queens decide to go to the Lord's temple, take flowers and sandal and the child with them, and set out.
event: The queens carry offerings and the baby to the temple.

tamil: சிறுவன்றன் சரணந் தீண்டச் சினாலயங் கதவு நீங்கப்
பிறைநுதற் றாதி தானும் பிள்ளைவிட் டுட்பு குந்தாள்
நறைமலர் வாவி தன்னு ணற்சுதன் வீழக் காணாச்
சிறையழி காதற் றாயுஞ் சென்றுடன் வீழ்ந்தா ளன்றே.
reading: As the child's foot touches it, the Jina temple's doors swing open; the queen leaves the child and goes in, and the boy falls into the flower pond, at which the mother, unable to bear it, plunges in after him.
nuance: The sage's sign in 46 (doors opening, the pond) is fulfilled; a mother's loving leap into water is given as plain feeling, with no comment on it.
event: The temple doors open at the infant's touch, he falls into the pond, and his mother leaps in after him.

tamil: கறைகெழு வேலி னான்றன் காரிகை நீர்மே னிற்பப்
பிறையெயிற் றரவின் மீது பெற்றிருந் தனையற் கண்டு
பறையிடி முரச மார்ப்பப் பாங்கினா லெடுத்து வந்து
இறைவனை வணங்கி யேத்தி யியன்மனை புகுந்தா னன்றே.
reading: Seeing the queen standing in the water and the child lying safe on the serpent's hood, the people carry him out to the sound of drums, bow to the Lord and go home.
event: The child is found on a serpent's hood and brought out with drums and worship.

tamil: நாகத்தின் சிரசின் மீது நன்மையிற் றரித்தென் றெண்ணி
நாகநற் குமர னென்று நரபதி நாமஞ் செய்தான்
நாகநே ரகலத் தானை நாமகட் சேர்த்தி யின்ப
நாகவிந் திரனைப் போல நரபதி யிருக்க மந்நாள்.
reading: Thinking him held kindly on the serpent's head, the king names him Nagakumaran; the Naga-chested one joins him with Lakshmi and lives like Nagendra, and then comes the day of the next episode.
nuance: Line 3 is obscure about who is joined with Nāmakal (நாமகள், the goddess of learning); the king's act of naming is plain.
event: The king renames the child Naga Kumaran because the serpent held him.

tamil: கின்னரி மனோக ரீயென் கெணிகைநற் கன்னி மாரும்
அன்னவர் தாயும் வந்தே யரசனைக் கண்டு ரைப்பார்
என்னுடைச் சுதையர் கீத மிறைவநின் சிறுவன் காண்க
reading: The courtesan girls Kinnari and Manokari and their mother come to the king and she asks him to hear her daughters' music, which he agrees to hear.
nuance: Whether கின்னரி and மனோகரி name two girls or a girl and her mother is not clear from the verse.
event: The courtesans and their mother present their daughters' song before the king and the prince.

tamil: இசையறி குமரன் கேட்டே யிளையவள் கீத நன்றென்
றசைவிலா மன்னன் றானு மதிசய மனத்த னாகித்
திசைவிளக் கனையாள் மூத்தாள் தெரிந்துநீ யென்கொ லென்ன
வசையின்றி மூத்தா டன்னை மனோகரி நோக்கக் கண்டேன்.
reading: The music-knowing prince finds the younger girl's song good, and the king, astonished, asks him which of the two is the elder, the answer given that Manokari looked at the elder without fault.
nuance: Lines 3-4 give the speakers' turns without marks; who says 'I saw Manokari look at the elder' is a guess.
event: The prince praises the younger singer; the king asks him about the elder.

tamil: பலகல மணிந்த வல்குற் பஞ்சநற் சுகந்த னீயும்
துலங்குதன் சுதையர் தம்மை தூய்மணிக் குமரற் கீந்தாள்
அலங்கல்வேற் குமரன் றானு மாயிழை மாதர் தாமும்
புலங்களின் மிகுத்த போகம் புணர்ந்தின்பக் கடலு ளாழ்ந்தார்.
reading: The mother gives her daughters to the pure-gemmed prince, and he and the women together sink into a sea of pleasure that fills the senses.
nuance: பஞ்சநற் சுகந்தன் is taken as the mother's name or title; the verse does not gloss it.
event: The mother gives her daughters to Naga Kumaran, and they enjoy pleasure together.

title: இரண்டாம் சருக்கம் 57-73 (2/2)
theme: The prince tames an elephant and a horse and masters learning; his stepmother-like rival's talk leads the king to order him away, and the prince answers by a show of riding, by winning at dice from kings and giving it back, so that the king builds him his own city of Alankarapuram.
source_issues: Verses 60 to 71 are hard to read: the text names no accuser or accusation, and several lines (60.3, 61.2-3, 63.2, 64.1, 69.2, 70.4) are corrupt or obscure.
Verse 69 ends with a stray full stop and semicolon.
Chapter 4 opens in the middle of a scene; verse 57 is the end of the elephant episode begun in the previous chapter's prophecy.

cast.role: the hero, son of Jayandhara and Prithivi-devi
the king of Rajamagriha, the prince's father (named in line 4 of verse 62)
a queen of the king (Visalakanni, Visalanetrai), who speaks of the prince's fame and is taken as accuser
Visalanetri's son, who plots after hearing of the prince's fame
the prince's mother, who tells him what has happened
the king's servants who report and carry out the seizure
the neighbouring kings who play dice with the prince

tamil: நாகமிக் கதங்கொண் டோடி நகர்மாட மழித்துச் செல்ல
நாகநற் குமரன் சென்று நாகத்தை யடக்கிக் கொண்டு
வேகத்தின் விட்டு வந்து வேந்தநீ கொள்க வென்ன
வாகுநற் சுதனை நோக்கி யானைநீ கைக்கொள் ளென்றான்.
reading: The prince goes after a maddened elephant that has been wrecking the city's mansions, subdues it, lets it go to the king, and the king bids his other son keep it.
nuance: The rut that the prince masters is the same maddened state (மதம்) that the sage's prophecy in verse 46 had named, so the feat reads as the fulfilment of a foretold sign. Line 3 and 4 do not make clear which son the king addresses (வாகுநற் சுதன்): the reading follows the word order.
event: Naga Kumaran subdues the elephant that has run amok in the city and offers it to the king, who tells his son to take it.

tamil: மற்றோர்நாட் குமரன் றுட்ட மாவினை யடக்கி மேற்கொண்
டுற்றவூர் வீதி தோறு மூர்ந்துதீக் கோடி யாட்டி
வெற்றிவேல் வேந்தற் காட்ட விழைந்துநீ கொள்க வென்றான்
பற்றியே கொண்டு போகிப் பவனத்திற் சேர்த்தி னானே.
reading: On another day the prince masters a vicious horse, rides it through every street with a fire-brand and shows it to the victorious king, who tells him to keep it; he takes it home.
nuance: Line 2 (தீக்கோடி ஆட்டி) is not clear; it is read here as a flourish with fire while riding.
event: Naga Kumaran tames a vicious horse, parades it through the streets and presents it to the king, who lets him keep it.

tamil: அறவுரை யருளிச் செய்த வம்முனி குறித்த நான்குந்
திறவதி னெய்தி நல்ல சீர்கலைக் கடலை நீந்திப்
படுமதக் களிறுந் தேர்மா புகழ்பெற வூர்ந்து மூன்றாம்
பிறையது போல்வ ளர்ந்து பீடுடைக் குமர னானான்.
reading: Having gained the four things the sage's teaching of dharma had pointed to, the prince crosses the sea of learning, rides elephants and chariot horses with renown, and grows like the waxing moon into a distinguished youth.
nuance: The 'four' (நான்கு) are not named in the verse; they are taken as the four things the sage foretold or set out in the earlier teaching. The verse ties worldly mastery to the sage's words and not to the prince's own effort alone.
event: Naga Kumaran grows up, masters the arts and the riding of elephants and horses, and comes of age.

tamil: தூசுநீர் விசாலக் கண்ணி சுதனைக்கண் டினிது ரைப்பாள்
தேசநற் புரங்க ளெங்குந் திகழ்பணி குமரன் கீர்த்திப்
பேசொணா வகையிற் கேட்டேன் பெருந்தவ மில்லை நீயும்
ஏசுற விகழொன் றின்றி யினியுனைக் காக்க வென்றாள்.
reading: Visalakanni, seeing her son, tells him kindly that she has heard the prince's fame spread beyond telling through all the lands, that she has no great merit, and that he should so act that no blame touches him and he be protected.
nuance: Line 3 (பெருந்தவம் இல்லை நீயும்) can be read as the speaker's own lack of merit or a charge that her son lacks it; the speaker's tone, kindly or envious, is not fixed. The son (சுதன்) is taken as Srithara, because verse 61 turns to him.
event: Visalanetri speaks to her son Srithara of Naga Kumaran's spreading fame.

tamil: சிரிதரன் கேட்டு நெஞ்சிற் செய்பொரு ளென்னென் றேகி
குறிகொண் டாயி ரத்தினோரைக் கொன்றிடு மொருவ னாகச்
செறியுமைஞ் ஞூறு பேருஞ் சீர்மையிற் கரத்தி னாரை
யறிவினிற் கூட்டிக் கொண்டு வமர்ந்தினி திருக்கு மந்நாள்.
reading: Srithara, hearing this, resolves in his heart what to do, and gathers five hundred men of skilled hands, one of whom is to be the killer of a thousand, and stays on happily until the day comes.
nuance: The lines on the thousand and five hundred are obscure; whether the men are assassins or a guard is not settled by the verse itself, and the plot is a reading from the next verses.
event: Srithara plans against Naga Kumaran and assembles five hundred skilled men.

reading: The prince and his fair wives bathe in the pond called Kuccam while a maid carries garlands, saffron and silk; meanwhile Jayandhara sits on the upper floor of his mansion.
event: Naga Kumaran bathes in the pond with his wives while the king watches from the upper floor.

reading: The king's queen Visalanetri comes to the pond's bank and stands there, and the prince bows to her on seeing her.
nuance: Line 2 speaks of a thief who couples with another's wife; it suggests a charge laid against the prince but the syntax is broken, so the accusation is only inferred from verses 64 and 65.
event: Visalanetri comes to the pond's bank where Naga Kumaran sees her and bows.

reading: The king rages at the woman who has spun falsehood, while the prince and his slender wife, adorned with garlands and sandal, go back with the attendant to their great house.
nuance: The verse says plainly that a lie was fabricated (பொய்யுரை புனைந்தவளை) but not who is accused or who lies; the king's anger may fall on the liar or on the person she slandered.
event: The king is enraged at the woman's lie; the prince and his wife return to their house.

reading: The king asks his queen where she had gone, why she went to watch her son bathe, why he plays with her in the house, and tells that he must go and play outside the city.
nuance: The addressee (தேவி) and whose son is meant are not clear; the verse is read as the king sending Naga Kumaran to live outside the capital, which verse 73 then carries out.
event: Jayandhara questions the queen and orders the prince out of the city to play.

reading: The king leaves after speaking; the queen bows her head, joyless and grieving; the prince, clever, comes in wonder and asks her, and on hearing the king's word he mounts an elephant.
event: The queen grieves at the king's order; Naga Kumaran asks her, hears of the order and mounts an elephant.

reading: With drums sounding, the prince subdues a rutting elephant and displays circling riding in every street to the sound of many instruments, and the king hears of the angry procession.
nuance: The prince's riding is a show of his mastery in the face of the order to leave; the verse does not say he is defying it, but the king takes it as such in verse 68.
event: Naga Kumaran parades on a rutting elephant through the streets and the king hears of it.

reading: Servants tell the king that the prince has overstepped his sweet word; the king bids them enter his house and take the golden ornaments and goods, and they seize them.
nuance: The verse gives no sign that the story judges the stripping unjust or just; it reports the king's order as an act of sceptre, and verses 69 to 72 show the prince turning it round by dice.
event: The king, told that the prince disobeyed, orders his house stripped of ornaments and goods, and the servants take them.

reading: The prince comes down from his elephant, his mother tells him what has happened, and he goes into the house to play at dice, beats the kings, and takes away the ornaments that gather.
nuance: The text of line 4 ends in a stray punctuation mark; the order of events is hard to fix.
event: On his mother's telling Naga Kumaran plays dice with the kings, beats them and carries off their ornaments.

reading: All the kings, at the great king's sight, bow, with serpent-gem necklaces, pearl garlands, bracelets and armlets, and a cry goes up about the matter.
nuance: Line 4 (வேந்தென்ன இக்கூற்றென) is corrupt or obscure; the sense is a guess.
event: The kings bow before the king with their jewels gathered.

reading: A speaker tells the king that by dice he has won the prince's ornaments, that the prince invited him to play and then, out of love for his father, beat him greatly in two games.
nuance: The speaker is not named; he is read as one of the kings who played, but the verse could also be the king's own account.
event: A king reports to Jayandhara that he won the prince's jewels at dice and then lost twice to him.

reading: The prince gives each king who had agreed to play the hereditary goods that rightly belong to them, returns home and hands the rest to his mother, and gives the kings their own necklaces back.
nuance: The dice are the means by which a prince put out of his goods wins goods back, and the story ends not in keeping them but in giving them away, which the Kural's warning on gambling does not allow for.
event: Naga Kumaran returns the kings' hereditary property and necklaces, and gives the rest to his mother.

reading: By the king's command a fine city is built outside the great city for the prince to live in, and it is called Alankarapuram; the youth wears a gold garland there.
event: Jayandhara orders a city built outside the capital where Naga Kumaran lives, named Alankarapuram.

title: மூன்றாம் சருக்கம் 74-87 (1/2)
theme: The story turns to Uttara Madurai: its king, told by a sage that his sons will serve another, gives them the crown and takes to the forest. The sons reach Pataliputra, marry there, meet Naga Kumara, and Vyala defeats an army sent against him. A minister ends Sridharan's anger, and the prince settles in Vyala's city.
source_issues: 80: the line 2-3 sense of தானவற்கு and தாதி is unclear and the allocation of brides is read by plain order.
76: the metre and a stray word அதிக in line 3 are normal, but the cast name செயவர் is read from 75.3 as a name.

cast.role: the prince, hero of the poem
king of Uttara Madurai, father of Vyala and Mahavyala
the sage who foretells the sons' future
one of the king's two sons, who befriends Naga Kumara
the other son, named with Vyala as வியாளமா வியாளர்
king of Pataliputra
an adversary whose army attacks Naga Kumara
a minister who carries the king's words
Naga Kumara's friend

tamil: அரிவையர் போகந் தன்னி லானநற் குமரன் றானும்
பிரிவின்றி விடாது புல்லிப் பெருமலர்க் காவு சேர்ந்து
பரிவுட னினிதி னாடிப் பாங்கினாற் செல்லு நாளில்
reading: The poet says the prince, bound to his pleasures with women, wanders happily from garden to garden, and then turns to tell what his companion brought to him.
event: Naga Kumara spends his days in pleasure gardens with women until his friend comes with news.

tamil: பாரணி சூர சேனம் பண்ணுதற் கரிய நாட்டுள்
ஊரணி கொடிக ளோங்கு முத்தர மதுரை தன்னில்
வாரணி கொங்கை மார்க்கு மாரனேர் செயவர் மாவின்
சீரணி தேவி நாமஞ் செயவதி யென்ப தாகும்.
reading: The story shifts to Uttara Madurai in the Surasena land, where the king's queen is named Jayavathi.

tamil: வேய்ந்தவெம் முலையாள் பக்கல் வியாளமா வியாள ரென்னுஞ்
சேர்ந்திரு புதல்வர் தோன்றிச் செவ்வியாற் செல்லு நாளில்
காந்திநற் றவத்தோர் வந்தார் கடவுணேர் தூம சேனர்
வேந்தன்வந் தடிவ ணங்கி விரித்தொன்று வினவி னானே.
reading: Two sons, Vyala and Mahavyala, are born to the queen, and when the sage Dhumasena comes the king bows and puts a question to him.
event: The sage Dhumasena visits the king of Uttara Madurai, who bows and asks him a question.

tamil: என்னுடையப் புதல்வர் தாமு மினியர சாளு மொன்றோ
அன்னியன் சேவை யொன்றோ வடிகணீ ரருளிச் செய்மின்
துன்னிய புதல்வர் தாமு மொருவனைச் சேவை பண்ணும்
என்றவர் குறியுஞ் சொல்ல யெழின்முடி புதல்வர்க் கீந்தான்.
reading: The king asks the sage whether his sons will rule or serve another, hears that they will serve one man, and gives them the crown.
nuance: The sage's answer is told only in outline; the verse does not name the man the sons will serve, so the prophecy is open until later verses.
event: Told by the sage that his sons will serve one man, the king crowns his sons.

tamil: மன்னன்போய் வனம டைந்து மாமுனி யாகி நிற்பப்
பின்னவ ரமைச்சன் றன்மேற் பெருநிலப் பாரம் வைத்துத்
தன்னிறை தேடிப் போந்தார் தரைமகட் டிலதம் போலும்
பன்னக நகர நேராம் பாடலி புரம தாமே.
reading: The king goes to the forest and stands as a great ascetic, while the sons leave the land's burden with a minister and go seeking a lord of their own at Pataliputra.
nuance: The king leaves only after he has put the crown on his sons, so renunciation follows the duty of rule rather than replacing it; the sons in turn hand the rule to a minister, and the verse does not say whether the leaving is by choice or by the sage's word.
event: The king becomes a forest ascetic and his sons leave the realm to a minister and travel to Pataliputra.

tamil: நன்னகர்க் கிறைவ னல்ல னாமஞ்சிரீ வர்ம னாகுந்
தன்னவன் றேவி பேருந் தக்கசிரீ மதியா மம்பொற்
கிண்ணம்போல் முலையாள் புத்ரி கேணிகாசுந் தரியென் பாளாம்
விண்ணுறை தேவர் போல வியாளமா வியாளர் வந்தார்.
reading: Pataliputra's king is Srivarman, his queen Srimathi and his daughter Kenikasundari, and the two brothers arrive there like gods from heaven.
event: Vyala and Mahavyala reach Pataliputra, whose royal family is introduced.

tamil: மன்ன னைக்கண் டிருப்ப மாவியாளன் றகமை கண்டு
தன்னுடையப் புதல்வி தன்னைத் தானவற் கொடுத்துத் தாதி
துன்னிய மகளி தன்னைச் சுந்தரி வியாள னுக்கு
மன்னியற் கொடுப்ப மன்ன ரிருவரு மின்புற் றாரே.
reading: The king of Pataliputra, seeing the brother's worth, gives his daughter to one and a maid's daughter Sundari to Vyala, so both kings are glad.
nuance: Who receives whom turns on the words தானவற்கு and தாதி துன்னிய மகள், which are not clear in the line; the reading follows the plain order and is not firm.
event: Srivarman gives his daughter to Mahavyala and the maid's daughter Sundari to Vyala.

tamil: சிறுதினஞ் சென்ற பின்பு சீருடன் வியாளன் போந்து
நறுமலர்க் கோதை வேலான் நாகநற் குமரற் கண்டு
சிறுமலர் நெற்றிக் கண்ணுஞ் சேரவே மறையக் கண்டு
சிறியன்யா னின்னா னென்றான் செல்வனு மகிழ்வுற் றானே.
reading: After a few days Vyala sees Naga Kumara and the small eye on his forehead is hidden, and he declares himself the lesser man, which pleases the prince.
nuance: Whether the hidden forehead eye is a mark Vyala recognises, and who says சிறியன் யான், depend on a few ambiguous words; the reading gives Vyala the speech.
event: Vyala meets Naga Kumara, sees the mark on his forehead and calls himself small, and the prince is glad.

tamil: செல்வனைக் கொல்வ தென்று சிரீதரன் சேனை வந்து
பல்சன மனையைச் சூழப் பண்புடை வியாளன் கண்டு
வல்லைநீர் வந்த தென்ன வள்ளலை வதைக்க வென்றார்
கொல்களி யானைக் கம்பங் கொண்டுடன் சாடி னானே.
reading: Sridharan's soldiers come to kill the lord and surround the house, and Vyala asks why they came and strikes them with an elephant-post.
nuance: The killing is done by one who guards a guest and the narrator calls Vyala well-mannered, so the slaughter is praised as loyalty rather than faulted as violence.
event: Sridharan's army surrounds the house to kill Naga Kumara and Vyala destroys it with an elephant tether-post.

tamil: சேனைதன் மரணங் கேட்டு சிரீதரன் வெகுண்டு வந்தான்
ஆனைமேற் குமரன் றோன்றி யவனும்வந் தெதிர்த்த போது
மானவேன் மன்னன் கேட்டு மந்திரி தன்னை யேவ
கோனவர் குமரற் கண்டு கொலைத் தொழி லொழித்த தன்றே.
reading: Hearing of his army's death Sridharan comes in anger, but when the prince appears before him on an elephant the king's minister is sent and the killing stops.
event: Sridharan attacks in anger; Naga Kumara faces him on an elephant and the king sends a minister to end the fighting.

tamil: நாகநற் குமரற் கண்டு நயந்தர னினிய கூறும்
வேகநின் மனைக்குச் சூரன் வெகுண்டவன் வந்தா னென்ன
போகநீ தேசத் தென்று புரவலன் சொன்னா னென்ன
ஆகவே யவன்முன் போகி லவ்வண்ணஞ் செய்வ னென்றான்.
reading: The minister Nayantaran gently tells the prince that the angry hero has come to his house and that the king wishes him to leave the land, and the prince says he will do to him as before if he meets him.
nuance: Whose command to leave, and who the angry hero is, depend on loose pronouns in lines 2 to 4; the verse leaves the prince's answer ambiguous.
event: Nayantaran warns Naga Kumara to leave and the prince refuses to avoid a fight.

tamil: நயந்தரன் சென்று ரைப்பா னல்லறி வின்றி நீயே
செயந்தனி லொருவன் கையிற் சேனைதன் மரணங் கண்டும்
நயந்தறி யாத நீயே நன்மனை புகுக வென்றான்
பயந்துதன் சேனை யோடும் பவனத்திற் சென்ற வன்றே.
reading: Nayantaran tells the enemy that he lacks sense, having seen his army killed by one man and still not understood, and bids him go home, so he goes frightened with his troops.
nuance: The advice is a minister's face-saving retreat for a defeated lord, framed as a rebuke; the verse does not say the lord is wrong to feel shamed.
event: Nayantaran sends Sridharan home with a rebuke and Sridharan withdraws with his army.

tamil: தந்தையா லமைச்சன் சொல்லத் தானுந் தன்றாய்க் குரைத்து
தந்திமேன் மாதர் கூடத் தோழனுந் தானு மேறி
நந்திய வியாள னன்னூர் மதுரை யிற்புக் கிருந்து
அந்தமி லுவகை யெய்தி அமர்ந்தினி தொழுகு நாளில்.
reading: On the minister's word from the father, the prince tells his mother, rides an elephant with the women and his friend, and settles happily in Vyala's Madurai.
event: Naga Kumara tells his mother and travels with friend and women to Vyala's city, where they live in joy.

reading: The prince, the king and the friend go to play outside the city and come upon five hundred young men with veenas, and the prince speaks to them.
event: Naga Kumara's party meets five hundred veena-playing youths outside the city.

title: மூன்றாம் சருக்கம் 88-101 (2/2)
theme: The prince beats the vina-skilled princess Tribhuvanarati, worships at a Jain shrine, frees a hunter's wife from a demon, gains gifts and the service of a yakshi, marries the daughter of Vanaraja and wins him a city, and the section ends on the king Somaprabha who loses his land and takes up the ascetic's yoga to end his deeds.
source_issues: The verse lines carry edition-specific spellings and unclear word division (e.g. வனராசன், இரம்மிய வேட னன்பேன்), and the daughter's name in 99 does not appear in the lines.

cast.role: the hero, a prince, called குமரன் in the verses
the prince's friend and companion
princess of Kampiram, skilled at the vina, won by the prince
the vina-learners who tell the prince about the princess
a merchant who tells the prince of a marvel
the hunter whose wife was taken to the cave
the demon who seized the hunter's wife
a vyantara god who gives the prince gifts
a yakshi of the Hiranya cave who offers her servants
a forest dweller (the hunter) who tells of marvels
a vyantara standing guard
king of Giripuram
Vanaraja's queen
a king who lost his land and became an ascetic

reading: Questions are put to the newcomers about where they live, who they are and where they are going, and one who knows them names their town and the names of their father and mother, saying they are learners of the vina.
nuance: The speakers of the question and of the answer are not named and the grammar of lines 2-4 is loose, so who answers and who is called vina-learners is a guess from the next verse.
event: Strangers are asked who they are and one answers for them, naming their home and parents.

tamil: நந்தன ராசன் றேவி நாமந் தாரணியாம் புத்திரி
கந்தமார் திரிபுவ னாரதி கைவீணை யதனிற் றோற்று
என்தம ரோடுங் கூட வெங்களூர்க் கேறச் சென்றோம்.
reading: The speakers say they come from the city Kampiram in the land Nandu-Kampira, whose king Nandana has a queen named Tharani and a daughter Tribhuvanarati, and that they and their kin have come to their own town because the princess's vina skill is boasted of.
nuance: Lines 3-4 are hard to construe (கந்தமார்... தோற்று); the sense that the princess is a vina champion whom others come to try is taken from verse 90, which has the prince defeat her on the vina.
event: The vina-learners tell the prince that the princess Tribhuvanarati of Kampiram is famed for her vina and that they went to her town.

tamil: வெற்றிவேற் குமரன் கேட்டு வியாள னுந் தானுஞ் சென்று
விற்புரு வதனத் தாளை வீணையின் வென்று கொண்டு
கற்புடை யவடன் காமக் கடலிடை நீந்து நாளில்
உற்றதோர் வணிக னைக்கண் டுவந்ததி சயத்தைக் கேட்டான்.
reading: The prince hears this, goes with Viyalan, beats the bow-browed princess at the vina and wins her, and while he swims in the sea of love with her he meets a merchant and asks about a wonder the man has seen.
nuance: The wager of the vina-contest is not stated in the verse; that defeat wins her is taken from வென்று கொண்டு.
event: Naga Kumara and Viyalan win Tribhuvanarati by defeating her at the vina, and Kumara then questions a merchant about a marvel.

tamil: தீதில்பூந் திலக மென்னுஞ் சினாலய மதனின் முன்னிற்
சோதிமிக் கிரணந் தோன்றுஞ் சூரிய னுச்சி காலம்
ஓதிய குரல னாகி யொருவனின் றலறு கின்றான்
ஏதுவென் றறியே னென்றா னெரிமணிக் கடகக் கையான்.
reading: At noon, before the Jain temple named Thilaka, a man with a ringing voice stands crying out, and the arm-braceleted one says he does not know the cause.
nuance: The speaker of line 4 is probably the merchant of 90, since he is the one asked about a wonder, but the verse does not say so.
event: A man is heard crying at the Jain shrine at noon and the merchant says he does not know why.

tamil: சென்றந்த வால யத்திற் சினவரற் பணிந்து நின்று
வென்றந்த விமலன் மீது விரவிய துதிகள் சொல்லி
முன்னந்த மண்ட பத்தின் முகமலர்ந் தினிதி ருந்தான்.
reading: Hearing it, the broad-shouldered prince goes into the shrine, bows to the Jina, praises the pure victor and sits at ease with a bright face in the front hall.
nuance: Lines 3-4 give the prince's worship as an act, not an argument; the claim is the worship's premise.
event: Naga Kumara enters the Jain temple, worships the Jina and sits in its mandapa.

tamil: பூசலிட் டொருவன் கூவப் புரவல குமரன் கேட்டு
ஓசனிக் கின்ற தென்ன வொருதனி நின்ற நீயார்
ஆசையென் மனைவி தன்னை யதிபீம வசுரன் கொண்டு
பேசொணா மலைமு ழஞ்சுட் பிலத்தினில் வைத்தி ருந்தான்.
reading: As a man cries out, the prince asks who he is, and the man says that the great demon Athibhima has seized his wife and shut her in a cave of burning mountain rock too awful to describe.
nuance: ஆசை in line 3 may be the wife's name or the word for desire; verse 94 resolves who speaks.
event: A husband begs help because the demon Athibhima holds his wife in a mountain cave.

tamil: இரம்மிய வனத்துள் வாழ்வே னிரம்மிய வேட னன்பேன்
விம்முறு துயர்சொற் கேட்டு வீரனக் குகைகாட் டென்னச்
செம்மையிற் சென்று காட்டச் செல்வனுஞ் சிறந்து போந்து
அம்மலைக் குகைவாய் தன்னி லண்ணலு முவந்து நின்றான்.
reading: The man says he lives in the forest as the hunter Rammiya, and at his sorrowful word the prince asks to be shown the cave and, when the hunter has led him, rejoices at the cave mouth.
nuance: The hunter's name is split across the line breaks of the edition; the reading Rammiya is from இரம்மிய வேட னன்பேன்.
event: The hunter leads Naga Kumara to the cave where his wife is held.

tamil: வியந்தர தேவன் வந்து வந்தனை செய்து நிற்ப
விந்தநற் கிராதன் றேவி தனைவிடு வித்த பின்புச்
சந்திர காந்தி வாளுஞ் சாலமிக் கமளி தானுங்
கந்தநற் காம மென்னுங் கரண்டகங் கொடுத்த தன்றே.
reading: A vyantara god comes and worships, the hunter's wife is freed, and the god gives the prince the Chandrakanti sword, a magical couch and a casket called Kamam.
nuance: Whether the god or the prince defeats Athibhima is not said; the demon is not named after 93 and the god's gift follows the release.
event: The vyantara god frees the hunter's wife and gives Naga Kumara a sword, a magic couch and a casket.

tamil: அங்குநின் றண்ணற் போந்து வதிசயங் கேட்ப வேடன்
இங்குள மலைவா ரத்தி லிரணிய குகையுண் டென்னக்
குங்கும மணிந்த மார்பன் குமரன்கேட் டங்குச் சென்றான்
அங்குள யியக்கி வந்து வடிபணிந் தினிது சொல்வாள்.
reading: As the prince goes on and asks about further marvels, the hunter says a Hiranya cave lies in the hill nearby, and the saffron-chested prince goes there, where a yakshi comes, bows at his feet and speaks sweetly.
event: Naga Kumara goes to the Hiranya cave and a yakshi greets him.

tamil: இனியுனக காள ரானோ மீரி ரண்டா யிரவர்
எனவவள் சொல்ல நன்றென் றினியொரு காரி யத்தின்
நினைவன்யா னங்கு வாவென் னீங்கிநற் குமரன் வந்து
வனசரன் றன்னைக் கண்டு வதிசயங் கேட்பச் சொல்வான்.
reading: The yakshi says that four thousand attendants are now at his service, he agrees and says he will think of her when there is a task and she is to come then, and he leaves and asks a forester to tell him of marvels.
nuance: ஈரிரண் டாயிரவர் is read as four thousand; the words ஈரிரண்டாயிரவர் could also be two thousands twice over, the same total, and the speaker of lines 2-3 is Kumara.
event: The yakshi offers Naga Kumara her four thousand servants and he promises to call them when needed.

tamil: வாள்கரஞ் சுழற்றி நிற்பான் வியந்தர னொருவ னென்னக்
காலினைப் பற்றி யீர்ப்பக் கனநிதி கண்டு காவ
லாளெனத் தெய்வம் வைத்து வருகனா லையத்துட் சென்று
தோளன தோழன் கூடத் தொல்கிரி புரத்தைச் சேர்ந்தான்.
reading: A forester tells of a vyantara who stands whirling a sword; the prince, dragged by the foot, sees great treasure and a god set there as guard, then goes through the temple with his strong-armed friend to Giripuram.
nuance: Who is pulled by the foot, and by whom, is not clear from the lines; the vyantara may be the treasure's guard or the tale told to the prince.
event: Naga Kumara finds a treasure guarded by a vyantara and then travels with his friend to the old city Giripuram.

tamil: அந்நகர்க் கதிப னான வனராசன் றேவி தானு
மன்னிய முலையி னாள்பேர் வனமாலை மகணன் னாமம்
பன்னரும் வேள்வி தன்னாற் பார்த்திபன் கொடுத்த தன்றே.
reading: The king of that city, Vanaraja, and his queen Vanamalai gave their daughter of the arrow-like eyes to Naga Kumara through a great sacrifice.
nuance: The daughter's name seems lost from line 2, where வனமாலை is the mother's name and மகள் நன்னாமம் is not followed by a name; the sacrifice (வேள்வி) is named as the means of the gift without comment.
event: Vanaraja gives his daughter in marriage to Naga Kumara at a sacrifice.

tamil: தாரணி வனரா சற்குத் தாயத்தா னொருவன் றன்னைச்
சீரணி குமரன் றோழன் சிறந்தணி மாமன் கூடப்
பாரணி வெற்றி கொண்டு புண்டர புரத்தை வாங்கி
யேரணி வனரா சற்கு யெழில்பெறக் கொடுத்த வன்றே.
reading: Naga Kumara, with his friend and his uncle, defeats a kinsman of Vanaraja and wins the city Pundarapuram, which he gives to Vanaraja.
event: Naga Kumara conquers Pundarapuram from Vanaraja's rival kinsman and hands it to Vanaraja.

tamil: சொல்லரு நாடி ழந்து சோமநற் பிரபன் போகி
யெல்லையிற் குணத்தின் மிக்க யெமதர ரடிவ ணங்கி
நல்லருட் சுரந்த ளிக்கு நற்றவ முனிவ னாகி
யொல்லையின் வினைகள் தீர யோகத்தைக் காத்து நின்றான்.
reading: Somaprabha loses his land, bows to the feet of a Jain teacher called Yamadhara, becomes a sage of great mercy and austerity, and stands guarding his yoga so that his old deeds may end.
nuance: The verse puts loss of the kingdom and the turn to renunciation side by side but does not say the loss caused the vow; that the vows end vinai is the narrator's own statement.
event: Somaprabha, who lost his kingdom, takes up the ascetic's life under a Jain teacher.

title: நான்காம் சருக்கம் 102-123 (1/2)
theme: The sage's prophecy to Jayavarma that his sons will serve another comes true when they leave home and join Naga Kumara, who then wins a bride, Gunavati, by relieving her father's city, and, going to the hill of the Vamana temple, sings a hymn that sets out the rewards of worship in rule, Indra's rank and release; a messenger from Kausambi then arrives with a letter and the names of the king's daughters.
source_issues: Verse 123 says seven daughters but names six.
Verse 105 and verse 116 have lines that are unclear in the printed text.
Verse 103 line 1 is obscure.

cast.role: king of Subhrathishta, who asks the sage about his sons and then gives up his kingdom
Jayavarma's two sons, who become Naga Kumara's servants
the supreme ascetic who foretells the sons' future
the great ascetic who settles in the grove with other sages
the hero, Naga Kumara
the five hundred men who take Naga Kumara as lord
king of the hill city Kirinagar, whose daughter Naga Kumara wins
Harivara's daughter, who becomes Naga Kumara's wife
the king who besieges Harivara's city for Gunavati
the lord of the Vamana temple on Urjayanta, praised in Naga Kumara's hymn
the archer-messenger who brings a letter from Kausambi

reading: The poet introduces Subhrathishta's ruler Jayavarma and his wife Jayavati, whose beauty is likened to a painted figure.
Jayavarma, living in great prosperity with his children, bows to a supreme ascetic of strict vows.
nuance: Line 1 (மக்கட் சேத்திய பேத்திய ரென்றிவர்) is obscure in the printed text; that the king's household and children are meant is inferred from the next verse.
event: Jayavarma bows low before a supreme ascetic.

reading: The king asks the sage whether his two sons will hold and rule his kingdom or serve another, and the sage answers that he will tell it.
nuance: The first three lines are the king's question; the last line gives the ascetic's reply in the poet's voice. The question treats the sons' future as something an ascetic's sight can read.
event: Jayavarma asks the ascetic whether his two sons will rule his kingdom or serve another, and the ascetic agrees to say.

reading: After the ascetic has spoken, the poet reports its sense: the sons will come to serve the protector who overthrows and drives out the ruler of Pundra.
nuance: The prediction is given in reported speech, not in the sage's own words, and the line naming who will serve whom is hard (கண்டிறந் துந்திடுங் காவலன்); that the conqueror is Naga Kumara is not said here and is known from the story.
event: The ascetic foretells that the king's sons will become servants of the king who defeats the ruler of Pundra.

reading: The king sets the land on his sons and stands to be rid of his remaining karma while the worthy sons take up the rule.
nuance: The abdication follows the prophecy, so the father leaves the sons to the fate the sage read and does not fight it. The words நிற்கும் செவ்வினை நீங்க நின்றனர் are the poet's only statement of why he leaves; செவ்வினை (here read as the deeds still to bear fruit) and the subject of நின்றனர் (the king, or king and queen) are not fixed.
event: Jayavarma hands his kingdom to his sons and takes up the ascetic's life to wear away his karma, and the sons rule.

reading: The great ascetic Somaprabha and endless virtuous sages settle in the fine grove of Subhrathishta.
event: Somaprabha and other sages take up residence in the grove of Subhrathishta.

reading: Jayavarma's sons bow at the sages' feet and say that this sage gave up the world because of the anger of Jayandhara's son.
nuance: It is not clear whether lines 3 and 4 are the princes' question (why did this sage renounce?) or an answer given to them, and who the Jayandhara's son is is not told in the verse. The story of the sage's loss is told elsewhere.
event: The princes bow to the sages and give anger of Jayandhara's son as the cause of the sage's renunciation.

tamil: என்றவ ருரையைக் கேட்டு இருவருந் துறந்து போந்து
சென்றுநற் குமரன் றன்னைச் சீர்பெற வணங்கிச் சொன்னார்
இன்றுமக் காள ரானோ மென்றவர் கூற நன்றென்
குன்றுசூழ் வனசா லத்துக் குமரன்சென் றிருந்த வன்றே.
reading: Having heard that account, the two brothers leave, go to Naga Kumara, bow, and say they are now his servants, which he accepts as he settles in the hill-ringed forest.
nuance: This is the story's fulfilment of the prophecy of verses 104 and 105: the sons who might have ruled serve the conqueror. The word துறந்து (leaving) is read here as leaving their home and kingdom, not necessarily taking up a monk's life.
event: The two princes go to Naga Kumara and become his servants, as the ascetic had foretold.

tamil: அடிமரத் திருப்ப வண்ண லந்நிழற் றிரித லின்றித்
கடிகமழ் மார்பன் றன்னைக் காத்துட னிருப்பப் பின்னும்
விடமரப் பழங்க ளெல்லாம் வியந்து நற்றுய்த் திருந்தார்
கொடிமலர்க் காவு தன்னுட் கோமக னிருந்த போழ்தில்.
reading: The princes stay at the tree's foot, never leaving its shade, and guard the prince, eating the fruits of the trees with admiration while he rests in the flowery grove.
nuance: விடமரப் பழங்கள் (fruit of poison trees?) is a doubtful reading; if it is right, the verse marks the princes' ease in eating fruit others would avoid.
event: The two princes stay beside Naga Kumara in a grove and guard him, living on the fruit.

tamil: அஞ்சுநூற் றுவர்கள் வந்தே யடிபணிந் தினிய கூறும்
தஞ்சமா யெங்கட் கெல்லாந் தவமுனி குறியு ரைப்ப
புஞ்சிய வனத்தி ருந்தோம் புரவல னின்னி டத்தின்
நெஞ்சிலிற் குறியன் காணா யெமக்குநீ றிறைவ னென்றார்.
reading: Five hundred men come, bow, and say that an ascetic told them the sign, that they have lived in the forest, and that they see his sign and take him as their lord.
nuance: The verse's last two lines are hard; the sense that the sage's sign (குறி) points to Naga Kumara as the lord they were promised is inferred.
event: Five hundred men come to Naga Kumara, accept him as their lord, and say a sage had told them his sign.

tamil: உரியநல் லவர்க ளோடு முவந்துட னெழுந்து சென்று
அரிவர னெதிர்க் கொண் டேக யவன்மனை புகுந்தி ருந்தான்.
reading: Naga Kumara rises gladly with his people on hearing of the hill city, goes to it, and is received by Harivara and enters his house.
event: Naga Kumara goes to the hill city, and its king Harivara receives him at his house.

tamil: அரிவர ராசன் றேவி யருந்ததி யனைய கற்பின்
மிருகலோ சனையென் பாளா மிக்கநன் மகடன் பேருஞ்
சுரிகுழற் கருங்கண் செவ்வாய்த் துடியிடைக் குணவ தீயைப்
பிரவிச் சோதன னிச்சித்துப் பெருநகர் வளைந்த தன்றே.
reading: Harivara's queen Mrigalochana, whose chastity was like Arundhati's, has a daughter Gunavati, and Pravichotana, desiring her, besieges the great city.
nuance: The queen's chastity is compared to the star Arundhati (the Cintamani uses the same measure at 327); the verse gives the comparison as an ornament and does not argue it. The desire (இச்சித்து) that drives the siege is the poem's cause of war.
event: Pravichotana, desiring Harivara's daughter Gunavati, surrounds his city with an army.

tamil: நாகநற் குமரன் கேட்டு நாற்படை யோடுஞ் சென்று
வேகநற் போர்க்க ளத்தில் வெற்றிகொண் டவனை யோட்டி
நாகநல் லெருத்தின் வந்து நகர்புகுந் திருப்ப மிக்க
போகமிக் குணவ தீயைப் புரவலன் கொடுத்த தன்றே.
reading: Naga Kumara hears of it, marches with his four-fold army, wins the battle, routs the besieger, enters the city on an elephant, and the king gives him Gunavati.
nuance: A guest repays the host's welcome of verse 112 by war, and the bride comes as the reward, not as a wooing.
event: Naga Kumara defeats Pravichotana and drives him off, and Harivara gives him his daughter Gunavati.

tamil: வேல்விழி யமிர்தன் னாளை வேள்வியா லண்ண லெய்திக்
கால்சிலம் போசை செய்யக் காமனும் ரதியும் போலப்
போனமும் போக மெல்லாம் பருகியின் புற்று நாளும்
நூனெறி வகையிற் றுய்த்தார் நுண்ணிடை துவள வன்றே.
reading: He takes the nectar-eyed girl in the marriage rite and, like Kama and Rati, they enjoy together the pleasures that the rules of the text allow, her anklets sounding.
nuance: நூனெறி (the way of the text) sets the limit on pleasure even as the verse compares the pair with the god of love; the verse does not say which text is meant.
event: Naga Kumara marries Gunavati and they live in pleasure.

tamil: கலையணி யல்குற் பாவை கங்குலும் பகலு மெல்லாஞ்
சிலையுயர்ந் தினிய திண்டோட் செம்மலும் பிரித லின்றி
நிலைபெற நெறியிற் றுய்த்தார் நிகரின்றிச் செல்லு நாளுள்
உலைதலி லுறுவ லீயா னூர்ச்சயந்த கிரிய டைந்தான்.
reading: The pair are never apart by night or day and enjoy life by the proper way, until the strong, unfailing prince goes to the hill of Urjayanta.
nuance: The hill is named only as ஊர்ச்சயந்த கிரி; that this is the sacred Jain hill and the 'Vamanar' of the next verse is Neminatha is the tradition's identification, not stated in these lines. The words உறுவலி ஈயான் (line 4) are unclear.
event: After days of constant union Naga Kumara goes to Urjayanta hill.

tamil: வாமனா லையத்து மூன்று வலங்கொண் டுட்புகுந் திறைஞ்சி
தாமமார் மார்பன் மிக்க தக்கநற் பூசை செய்து
சேமமா முக்கு டைக்கீ ழிருந்தரி யாச னத்தின்
வாமனார் துதிகட் சொல்ல வாழ்த்துபு தொடங்கி னானே.
reading: He circles the Vamana temple three times, enters, bows, worships well under the three umbrellas, and begins to praise the lord on the lion throne.
event: Naga Kumara worships at the Vamana temple on Urjayanta and begins a hymn to its lord.

reading: Those who bow with victory at the feet of the lord under the pearl umbrellas will rule the heaven, then rule all this earth on a great elephant under a white umbrella.
nuance: The promised fruit is rule, in heaven and then on earth, and not release; the hymn builds up in these three verses from kingship (118) to Indra-rank (119) to release (120).

reading: Those who worship in love the golden feet of the lord who sits on a lotus will go to the gods' world as Indras and be worshipped by the gods.
nuance: The lotus on which the lord sits (கமல மலர் மீதுறையும்) is the verse's one image, and the tirthankara is not named.

reading: Those who bow and praise the lord on the lion throne will be gods above gods, worshipped by the three worlds, and reach sweet release with the soul shining.
nuance: The worshipper's own soul shines in release (எரிபொன் உயிர் விளங்கி) and the verse does not say the lord gives it by grace; the worshipper's bowing is the stated cause.

reading: After praising the lord, Naga Kumara sits with his friends, and an archer sets a letter before him, joins his hands, bows, and speaks.
event: An archer brings a letter to Naga Kumara, bows, and begins to speak.

reading: The messenger names Kausambi in Vatsa country, its king Subhachandra, fiercer than foes, and his queen Sukavati, chaste like a mountain.
nuance: The messenger's account runs across the verses 122 to 123 and goes on after; the speaker is known from 121.

reading: The king and queen's seven daughters are named: Suyambhiraba, Nagasubhaprabha, Inbaprabha, Sornamalai, Padumai and Nagadattai.
nuance: The verse says seven daughters but names six; the seventh is lost or named in the next verse.

title: நான்காம் சருக்கம் 124-144 (2/2)
theme: The hero goes on winning wives by his mantra-rite (Menaki of Ujjayini, Srimati of Madurai, Madanamanjari, Ilakkanai), kills the Vidyadhara Vayuvegan who killed the Prithivitilaka king and seized his five hundred daughters, and at the end meets a sage and asks him the cause of his fortune.
source_issues: Verse 124 to 125 have corrupt lines (124 lines 1-2, 125 line 3) and the story cannot be fixed from them.
Verses 129 and 130 do not say plainly whose brother Mavyalan is, or who asks the question in 130.
Verse 128 line 3 was repaired by the build (pulli after a vowel sign removed).

cast.role: the hero, who wins brides by the mantra-rite
the hero's brother or companion of Pataliputra, who tells him of Menaki
daughter of King Jayasena of Ujjayini
the merchant who tells of Bhutilaka
the leader of the five hundred singing Vidyadhara women
the Vidyadhara who kills the women's father and seizes the kingdom
the five hundred brothers of the women, who become the hero's servants
the ancient sages who come to the grove
the Charana sage who teaches the hero dharma

reading: A verse whose first half is too corrupt to follow says that someone, after seeing a flaw, came and, failing to get the women he asked for, killed the king of the city of the white banner.
nuance: The first two lines are unclear (மேகவா கனன்றுரந்திட, கள்ளவிழ் மாசுகண்டனவன்) and the subject of the killing is not named; whether it is a foe of the hero, an earlier episode retold, or the hero himself cannot be fixed here.
event: An unnamed figure kills the king of the white-bannered city after failing to obtain the women he asked for.

reading: The king's younger brother, wanting the hero, sends a letter; once the hero has understood what the letter says, he turns the peacock-feathered arrow and kills the man who came.
nuance: The line breaks and the word நாந்தக (a sword name elsewhere) make the sense of lines 2 to 3 uncertain; who sent the letter and who is killed is read from the sentence order only.
event: The hero reads the letter brought to him, reworks an arrow and kills the man who had come with it.

reading: Going secretly to Abhichandra's city on an auspicious day, the hero marries the daughters of Subhachandra and Abhichandra's own daughter Sukanda by means of a mantra-rite, and is glad.
nuance: வேள்வி here is a rite performed with mantras (செபமந்திர வேள்வி) to win the women, not a Vedic sacrifice; the poem uses it again at 131, 139, 141 and 143 as the hero's way of taking brides.
event: The hero goes to Abhichandra's city and marries Subhachandra's daughters and Abhichandra's daughter by a mantra-rite.

reading: With the women as his companions the hero, joyful, takes his pleasure and plays on the pleasure-hill outside the swelling city.
event: The hero enjoys himself with his wives at a pleasure-hill outside the city.

reading: The text introduces Ujjayini in the land of Avanti, its king Jayasena, his wife Jayasri and their golden-hued daughter Menaki.
nuance: The last line names the daughter without a verb: the sentence is left open and finished in 129 to 131.

reading: Mavyalan of Pataliputra has come to Ujjayini; a Vidyadhara woman (சேடி) comes to tell Menaki of him, and she sees him and goes to the garden-wall of the treasure-city.
nuance: Who goes to the wall (நன்னிதிப் புரிசை) and why is not clear from the Tamil: நன்னிதி may be a name or an epithet, and the second half may refer to Menaki or to a different woman.
event: Mavyalan arrives in Ujjayini, and Menaki, told of him by a Vidyadhara woman, goes to him.

reading: Mavyalan leaves that city, goes to his elder brother and bows at his feet, and when the younger brother is asked where the hero is, he answers.
nuance: Line 3 to 4 make the pairing of 'elder brother' and 'hero' unclear: the Tamil can be read as the hero himself being the elder brother, and the questioner is not named.
event: Mavyalan leaves Ujjayini, bows to his elder brother and is asked about Nagakumara.

reading: Mavyalan tells of Menaki, slender-waisted and like the love-god's own beauty, and the hero goes to that city and weds her by the mantra-rite.
nuance: Mavyalan's words are the report of Menaki's beauty in lines 1 to 2; the marriage in lines 3 to 4 is the narrator's.
event: The hero hears from Mavyalan of Menaki, goes to Ujjayini and marries her by a mantra-rite.

reading: Another tale is told of Madurai, where the dancer Srimati, skilled in the drama and its victorious drums, has declared that whoever overcomes her will be her husband.
nuance: The speaker of line 1 (மற்றுமொன்று உரைத்தனன்) is not named; he is taken to be Mavyalan from 131. The last line is the sense of a challenge (பதியாம் பார்மிசை) and rests on a damaged word division.
event: A tale is told of the Madurai dancer Srimati, who will take as husband the man who defeats her.

reading: The hero goes there, beats her and takes her, lives with the women, then asks a merchant come by ship to tell him where a wonder is to be found.
nuance: The hero's question is in lines 3 and 4 (எங்குள அதிசயம் இயம்புக நீ).
event: The hero defeats Srimati and takes her, then asks an arriving merchant about marvels.

reading: The merchant answers that on the sea stands Bhutilaka, a city whose temple of the Lord has five hundred women singing daily as instructed, and he does not know why.
nuance: புங்கவன் (the Lord) is the Jina by the poem's frame (the temple is called அருகனாலயம் in 136), but the verse does not say so.
event: The merchant tells of a sea-island city where five hundred women sing daily at a temple.

reading: Remembering his own vidya, the hero goes with his chosen friends to the island, sees and circles the golden temple, and bows before the Jina.
nuance: வள்ளல் is the hero; the vidya he calls to mind (வித்தை) is the learned flying power by which he crosses the sea, though the verse does not say what it does.
event: The hero, with companions, flies to the island, circles the golden temple and worships.

reading: The hero, hearing the women sing in a line, calls them over and asks who they are to cry out before the Arhat temple, and Dharanisundari answers.
nuance: தரணிசுந் தரி is split across words by the edition; the speaker form in line 4 is as written.
event: The hero summons the singing women and asks who they are; Dharanisundari begins to answer.

reading: Dharanisundari says they are from the Vidyadhara city Prithivitilaka on the great silver mountain, where Vayuvegan asked their father to give them to his nephew.
nuance: மருகன் (nephew or son-in-law) leaves open whether the women were to marry Vayuvegan's nephew; the sentence at line 3 is loosely joined.
event: Dharanisundari tells where she and the others come from and that Vayuvegan demanded them for his nephew.

reading: Because their father refused, she says, Vayuvegan raged like fire, killed him, seized their kingdom and settled in the forest, and on hearing this the hero kills Vayuvegan.
nuance: The verse treats the hero's killing as the answer to Vayuvegan's, without remark; the poem does not ask whether the Jain rule against killing bears on it.
event: Vayuvegan, refused, kills the women's father and seizes the kingdom; the hero then kills Vayuvegan.

reading: The hero wins the five hundred women by the mantra-rite and enjoys them with love, and their five hundred brothers come as his servants and, worshipping him as refuge, live content.
event: The hero marries the five hundred Vidyadhara women, and their brothers become his attendants.

reading: The text introduces Ratnapura in Kalinga, its king Chandragupta, queen Chandramati and their daughter Madanamanjari.
nuance: Like 128 and 142, a city-and-king introduction with no verb.

reading: By the mantra-rite the hero reaches Madanamanjari, rides in her company and drinks deeply of her, their union like that of a nagas' pair.
nuance: The simile of the last line (நாகநற் புணர்ச்சிபோல்) plays on the hero's name Naga; the line 3 phrase தான்லயப் பருகினான் is read as drinking in desire.
event: The hero marries Madanamanjari by a mantra-rite and enjoys her.

reading: The text introduces Tilakapura in the land of Kangala, its king Vijayandhara and his wife Iyalvisai.
nuance: Another introduction in the series of city-and-king verses (128, 140, 142).

reading: The hero goes to Ilakkanai, their daughter, wins her at once by the rite and takes her pleasure, when ancient sages come to the grove.
nuance: The mantra-rite is called a matter of truth (மெய்ம்மை வேள்வி), the poem's claim that this is a true way of winning a bride.
event: The hero marries Ilakkanai and enjoys her; ancient sages arrive at the grove.

reading: The hero bows to the sage of firm austerity, hears the dharma that suits him, and asks what the high pleasure of Ilakkanai has been, which the sage will explain.
nuance: The sage's answer is not in this verse (the sentence ends with the promise to teach); the question is about the cause of that fortune in a former birth, as the next verses will show, but this verse says only ஏற்றமோகம் என்ன.
event: The hero bows to the Charana sage, hears dharma and asks about his pleasure with Ilakkanai.

title: ஐந்தாம் சருக்கம் 145-157 (1/2)
theme: The sage tells the hero his past birth as the merchant's son Nagadattan, who took the fast unto death and was reborn a god and then a king; the hero takes the same vow, goes to his father, and the father crowns him and leaves the world.
source_issues: Verse 145 line 3 and verse 148 line 4 are unclear; the merchant's second name and the day named in 148 cannot be fixed.
Verse 151 gives a calendar of months and days that cannot be taken apart with certainty.
Verses 156 and 157 overlap: both end with the father's handing on the throne and leaving.

cast.role: the hero, the former Nagadattan
the sage who tells the hero his past birth
Dhanadattan's wife, mother of Nagadattan
merchant's son of the past birth, who fasts unto death
the merchant's daughter, Nagadattan's wife
the ascetic who receives Nagadattan's vow
the minister who carries the father's summons
the hero's father, the king
the hero's wife

tamil: நாவலந் தீவு தன்னுள் நன்கயி ராவ தத்தின்
மேவுமின் முகில்சூழ் மாட வீதசோ கப்பு ரத்துக்
காவிநன் விழிமா தற்குக் காமன்விக் கிரம ராசன்
தாவில் சீர் வணிகன் நாமந் தனதத்த னென்ப தாமே.
reading: The telling of an earlier birth begins in a city of Jambudvipa, where a merchant named Dhanadattan lives.
nuance: The third line (காவிநன் விழிமா தற்குக் காமன்விக் கிரம ராசன்) is not clear: it may name the merchant's wife or give a second name or title, and the city's name is split across lines. The sage is the speaker only because the story is later said (150) to be told by an ascetic; this verse does not say so.

tamil: மனைவிதன் றனதத் தைக்கு மகனாக தத்த னாகும்
வனைமலர் மாலை வேலான் மற்றொரு வணிகன் றேவிப்
புனைமலர்க் கோதை நல்லாட் பொற்புடை வசும திக்கு
மனையினன் மகடன் னாம மியன்நாக வசுவென் பாளம்.
reading: Dhanadattan and his wife Dhanadattai have a son, Nagadattan, and another merchant and his wife Vasumati have a daughter, Nagavasu.
nuance: Nagadattan is, by the sage's own account in 149 and 150, an earlier birth of the hero; the hero is not named in this verse, so the identification is read from 150.
event: A son is born to the merchant couple, and the daughter Nagavasu is named in another merchant's house.

tamil: நண்புறு நாக தத்த னாகநல் வசுவென் பாளை
யன்புறு வேள்வி தன்னா லவளுடன் புணர்ந்து சென்றான்
பண்புறு நற்ற வத்தின் பரமுனி தத்த நாமர்
இன்புறும் புறத்தின் வந்தா ரிறைவனா லையத்தி னுள்ளே.
reading: Nagadattan marries Nagavasu and goes with her, and a great ascetic named Datta arrives in the king's temple grounds.
nuance: வேள்வி (line 2) is read as the marriage rite; the word could also mean a sacrifice, but no sacrifice follows.
event: Nagadattan, married to Nagavasu, meets the ascetic Datta who has come to the temple.

tamil: நாகதத் தன்சென் றந்த நன்முனி சரண டைந்து
வாகுநற் றருமங் கேட்டு அனசன நோன்பு கொண்டான்
போகபுண் ணியங்க ளாக்கும் பூரண பஞ்ச மீயில்
ஏகனற் றினத்தி னன்று யிடர்பசி யாயிற் றன்றே.
reading: Nagadattan takes refuge with the sage, hears the dharma and takes the fast unto death on the fifth day, when hunger and pain come.
nuance: Line 4 (ஏகனற் றினத்தி னன்று) is unclear; it is read as the day on which the pain of hunger came. The sage's teaching is not summarised, only its effect.
event: Nagadattan goes to the sage, hears the teaching and undertakes the fast unto death (அனசன நோன்பு).

tamil: தருமநற் றியானந் தன்னாற் றன்னுடை மேனி விட்டு
