வள்ளலு மகிழ்ந்து கேட்டு மாமுடி துளக்கி னானே.
reading: The great ascetics tell that the Vidyadharas of the silver mountain will take the whole world under a bright wheel, and the generous king listens gladly and nods his head.
nuance: Only the Vidyadharas' rule is named; that this refers to Udayanan's son is carried over from the previous verse.
event: Ascetics foretell that the Vidyadharas will rule the world under a bright wheel, and Udayanan gladly accepts it.

tamil: என்றவ ருரைப்பக் கேட்டே யிறைஞ்சிநன் கடிப ணிந்து
சென்றுதன் கோயில் புக்குச் சேயிழை பதுமை தன்னே
டொன்றினன் மகிழ்ந்து சென்னா ளுருமண்ணு வாவு முன்பு
வென்றிவேன் மகதன் மாந்த ரால்விடு பட்டி ருந்தான்.
reading: He bows to their feet, returns to his palace and joins Padumai in joy; at that time Urumannuvan has already been freed by the Magadha king's men.
nuance: The second half turns suddenly to Urumannuvan's release, which the verse does not explain.
event: Udayanan bows to the sages and goes to Padumai, while Urumannuvan has been released by the Magadha men.

tamil: மீண்டவன் வந்தூர் புக்கு வேந்தனை வணங்கி நிற்பக்
காண்டறி வாள னென்றே காவலன் புல்லிக் கொண்டு
மாண்டவன் வந்த தொப்ப வரிசையின் முகமன் கூறி
வேண்டவாந் தனிமை தீர்ந்தே விரகுட னின்புற் றானே.
reading: Urumannuvan returns, enters the city and bows to the king, who embraces him as one come back from the dead, greets him with due honour and ends his loneliness with rejoicing.
nuance: The word read here as the king's name for him, காண்டறிவாளன், is uncertain.
event: Urumannuvan returns and Udayanan embraces him and welcomes him.

tamil: வாரணி கொங்கை வேற்கண் வாசவ தத்தை தானும்
ஊரணி புகழி னான யூகியு மற்றுள் ளாரும்
தாரணி கொடியி லங்குஞ் சயந்தியி னின்றும் போந்து
பாரணி கோசம் பிப்பாற் பன்மலர்க் காவுள் வந்தார்.
reading: Vasavadatta, Yugi and the others leave Jayanti and come into the flower grove near Kausambi.
event: Vasavadatta, Yugi and their company leave Jayanti and enter a grove by Kausambi.

tamil: நயந்தநற் கேண்மை யாளர் நன்கமைந் தமைச்சர் தம்முள்
வயந்தக னுரைப்பக் கேட்டு வந்தவன் காவு சேரப்
பயந்தவ ரடியில் வீழப் பண்புடன் றழுவிக் கொண்டு
வியந்தர சியம்பு நீங்கள் வேறுடன் மறைந்த தென்னை.
reading: Vayantakan tells the king, who comes to the grove; they fall at his feet, he embraces them kindly and asks in wonder why they hid themselves.
nuance: The question is asked of the group; the next verse answers it in one man's voice.
event: Udayanan is told by Vayantakan, comes to the grove, embraces the fugitives and asks why they hid.

tamil: இருநில முழுதும் வானு மினிமையிற் கூடி னாலும்
திருநில மன்ன ரன்றிச் செய்பொரு ளில்லை யென்று
மருவுநூ னெறியி னின்றி வன்மையாற் சூழ்ச்சி செய்தேன்
அருளுடன் பொறுக்க வென்றா னரசனு மகிழ்வுற் றானே.
reading: The speaker says that though earth and sky may all unite sweetly, nothing is done without the kings, and so he left the way of the treatises and plotted by force, and asks pardon; the king is glad.
nuance: The speaker is taken to be Yugi from the answer to the question in verse 197; the second line is hard to construe.
event: A minister confesses that he used a plot against the treatises' way and asks pardon, and Udayanan is pleased.

tamil: ஆர்வமிக்க கூர்ந்து நல்ல வற்புதக் கிளவி செப்பிச்
சீர்மைநற் றேவி யோடுஞ் செல்வனு மனைபு குந்தே
ஏர்பெறும் வாச வெண்ணெ யெழிலுடன் பூசி வாச
நீர்மிக வாடி மன்ன னேரிழை மாதர்க் கூட.
reading: With fond and wondrous words the king goes into the house with his queen, anoints himself with fragrant oil and bathes, while fair-jewelled women attend.
nuance: The queen meant is not named and could be Vasavadatta or Padumai.
event: Udayanan and his queen go into the house, where the king is anointed and bathes.

tamil: யூகியு நீரி னாடி யுற்றுட னடிசி லுண்டான்
நாகநேர் கால மன்ன னன்குட னிருந்த போழ்தின்
பாகநேர் பிறையா நெற்றிப் பதுமையு மிதனைச் சொல்வாள்
ஏகுக செவ்வித் தந்தை யெழின்மனைக் கெழுக வென்றாள்
reading: Yugi bathes and eats his meal; as the king sits in happy company, Padumai tells him to go to the house of the other lady.
nuance: Where she sends him, and the word செவ்வித் தந்தை, are not clear.
event: Yugi bathes and eats, and Padumai bids Udayanan go.

tamil: என்றவள் சொல்ல நன்றென் றெழின்முடி மன்னன் போந்து
சென்றவண் மனைபு குந்து செல்வனு மிருந்த போழ்தின்
வென்றிவேற் கண்ணி னாளும் வெகுண்டுரை செப்பு கின்றாள்
கன்றிய காமம் வேண்டா காவல போக வென்றாள்.
reading: As the king sits in the other lady's house, she angrily tells him that her fierce desire is no longer wanted and he should go.
nuance: She is not named; she is taken to be Vasavadatta because the next verse calls her the sulking queen.
event: Vasavadatta, angry, tells Udayanan to leave.

tamil: பாடக மிரங்கும் பாதப் பதுமையி னோடு மன்னன்
கூடிய கூட்டந் தன்போற் குணந்தனை நாடி யென்ன
நாடினின் றனக்கன் னாடா னந்திணை யல்ல ளென்றான்
reading: The king, who has just been with Padumai, tells the sulking queen that on searching her qualities by feeling and by light, the other is not her equal.
nuance: The second half of the speech is obscure.
event: Udayanan tells the angry queen that Padumai is not her equal.

tamil: நங்கைதன் மனங்க லங்கா நலம்புகழ்ந் தூட னீக்கி
வெங்களி யானை மற்றப் பிடியொடு மகிழ் வதேபோற்
பொங்கிள முலையில் வாசப் பூசுசாந் தழியப் புல்லிச்
சிங்கவே றனைய காளை செல்வியைச் சேர்ந்தா னன்றே.
reading: He praises her beauty, wins her out of her sulk, and, like a rutting elephant with its mate, embraces her till the scented paste on her breasts is rubbed away.
nuance: The reconciliation works by praise first and the embrace after.
event: Udayanan praises Vasavadatta, ends her sulk and embraces her.

tamil: உருவிலி மதன்க ணைக ளுற்றுடன் சொரியப் பாய
இருவரும் பவளச் செவ்வா யின்னமிர் துண்டு வேல்போல்
திருநெடுங் கண்சி வப்ப வடிச்சிலம் போசை செய்ய
மருவிய வண்டு நீங்க மலர்க்குழல் சரிய வன்றே.
reading: Under the arrows of bodiless Madan the two drink the sweet nectar of each other's lips, their long eyes redden, anklets sound, bees fly off and the hair comes loose.
event: Udayanan and Vasavadatta unite in love.

title: வத்தவ காண்டம் 205-223 (2/3)
theme: Udayanan rewards his ministers, receives Pradyotan's letter owning the snare and asking pardon, sends Yugi to Ujjain where he is honoured and married to two brides, and returns to watch a ball-play at court.
source_issues: Verse 221: the e-text prints the verse without its number; it stands between 220 and 222.
Verse 206 line 4: the bride's name and who gives her are not clear.
Verse 212 line 1: the sense of கோடல் is doubtful.
Verse 218: the sister's name is doubtful and the sentence runs into verse 219.
Verse 223 line 3: hard to read.

tamil: கோதையும் சுண்ணத் தாதுங் குலைந்துடன் வீழ மிக்க
காதலிற் கழுமி யின்பக் கரையழிந் தினிதி னோடப்
போதவும் விடாது புல்லிப் புரவல னினிய னாகி
ஏதமொன் றின்ரிச் செங்கோ லினிதுடன் செலுத்து நாளில்.
reading: Wreaths and perfumed powder fall in disorder as Udayanan, steeped in love, holds Vasavadatta close and, kind and faultless, governs with a straight sceptre.
event: Udayanan lives in love with Vasavadatta and rules justly.

tamil: ஆனதன் னாம மிட்ட வாழிமோ திரத்தை யீந்தே
ஊனுமிழ் கதிர்வேன் மன்ன னுருமண்ணு வாவு தன்னைச்
சேனைநற் பதிநீ யென்று திருநிகர் பதுமை தோழி
ஈனமி லிராச னையை யெழில்வேள்வி யாற்கொ டுத்தான்.
reading: The king gives a ring bearing his own name and the post of army chief to Urumannuvan, and gives a woman named in the verse in marriage at a fair sacrifice; the last line is hard to read.
nuance: The woman given in marriage in line 4 is named only by a word the verse does not make clear, and the giver of the bride may be Padumai's friend named in line 3.
event: Udayanan rewards Urumannuvan with a ring and the command of the army.

tamil: சயந்தியம் பதியுஞ் சால விலாவாண நகரு மீந்தே
இயந்தநல் லிடப கற்கு மினியபுட் பகத்தைச் சூழ்ந்த
செயந்தரு வளநன் னாடு சிறந்தவைம் பதும ளித்து
வயந்தகன் றனக்கு வாய்ந்த பதினெட்டூர் கொடுத்தா னன்றே.
reading: Udayanan gives the cities Jayanti and Ilavanam, the rich land round Pushpakam and fifty more, and eighteen towns to Vayantakan.
event: Udayanan rewards Vayantakan and others with towns and lands.

tamil: ஆதிநன் மாமன் வைத்த வருந்திறை யளக்கு நல்ல
சேதிநன் னாட்டை யூகிக் காகநற் றிறத்தி னீந்து
சோதிநல் லரசன் மிக்க சூழ்ச்சியின் மற்றோர்க் கெல்லாம்
வீதிநன் னகர்கள் விட்டு வீறுடன் வீற்றி ருந்தான்.
reading: He gives the Cheti country, once set by his uncle as a tribute-paying land, to Yugi, and with clever counsel leaves the other towns free and sits in glory.
event: Udayanan gives the Cheti country to Yugi and rules in peace.

tamil: பேசரும் பெருமை சால்ப்ரச் சோதனன் றூதர் வந்து
வாசகந் தன்னைக் காட்ட வந்தவன் மனம கிழ்ந்து
வாசவ தத்தை யோடு மன்னிய வமைச்சர் கூட
வாசகஞ் சொல்க வென்று வரிசையிற் கேட்கின் றானே.
reading: Envoys of the great Pradyotan arrive and show his letter; Udayanan, glad, asks that the message be read, with Vasavadatta and his ministers beside him.
event: Pradyotan's envoys bring a letter, and Udayanan has it read before Vasavadatta and his ministers.

tamil: பிரச்சோத னன்றா னென்னும் பெருமக னோலை தன்னை
உரவுச்சேர் கழற்கான் மிக்க உதயண குமரன் காண்க
வாவுச்சீர்க் குருகு லத்தின் வண்மையான் கோடல் வேண்டி
வரைவனச் சார றன்னில் வன்பொறி யானை விட்டேன்.
reading: The letter, in Pradyotan's name, greets the king and says that, wishing to win the generosity of the Kuru line, he had set a cunning elephant in the mountain forest.
nuance: Here the king of Ujjain himself owns to the trick that Yugi's counsel had once matched with a false elephant of its own; the letter treats it as a way of winning a worthy man.
event: Pradyotan's letter admits that the elephant in the forest was his snare.

tamil: கலந்தவை காண வந்த காவலர் நின்னைப் பற்றிச்
சிலந்திநூ றன்னா லார்த்த சிங்கம்போ லார்த்துக் கொண்டு
நலந்திகழ் தேரி னேற்றி நன்குவுஞ் சையினி தன்னிற்
பெலந்திரி சிறையில் வைத்த பிழையது பொறுக்க வென்றும்.
reading: The letter goes on: the guards who came to see the thing seized you with spider's thread like a lion, set you on a chariot and shut you in the prison; pardon the fault.
nuance: The speaker is carried on from verse 210; the verse itself does not name him.
event: The letter admits Udayanan's seizure and imprisonment and asks pardon.

tamil: கோமானே யெனவே யென்னைக் கோடனீ வேண்டு மென்றும்
மாமனான் மருக னீயென் மாமுறை யாயிற் றென்றும்
ஆமாகும் யூகி தன்னை யனுப்ப யான் காண்டல் வேண்டும்
பூமாலை மார்ப வென்றும் பொறித்தவா சகத்தைக் கேட்டான்.
reading: The letter asks to be taken as lord, pleads the tie of uncle and nephew, asks that Yugi be sent so that the writer may see him, and Udayanan hears the sealed message.
nuance: The first line is hard to construe, and it is not clear whether the writer asks to be taken as king or as kin.
event: Udayanan hears the end of the letter, which asks him to send Yugi.

tamil: மன்னவ னனுப்ப யூகி மாநக ருஞ்சை புக்கு
மன்னிய வுவகை தன்னான் மகிழ்வுரை விளம்பி னானே.
reading: At the king's sending Yugi goes to Ujjain and bows to its king; the king nods his crowned head, looks long at the minister and speaks words of joy.
event: Yugi, sent by Udayanan, goes to Ujjain and is greeted gladly by Pradyotan.

reading: The king bids a drum be sounded through the city: Ujjain and Kausambi are two cities of one earth and he wants no distinction made between them.
event: Pradyotan has it proclaimed by drum that Ujjain and Kausambi are not to be distinguished.

reading: Yugi speaks lovingly of dharma texts with Salankayan; the king, finding such a man hard to get, rejoices in the minister.
event: Yugi and Salankayan talk of dharma texts and Pradyotan is pleased with Yugi.

reading: The king declares that Yugi's breadth, his pleasant look, his subtle counsel and the firmness of his word are such that no other man can match him, and his virtue has no bound.
event: Pradyotan praises Yugi as unmatched among men.

reading: The king, pleased, speaks of the rule fit for those who have such a man and adds that without such men there is no kingship.
nuance: The king who says this had been the captor of Yugi's lord, and the work lets him say it as praise of the man who has just outwitted him.
event: Pradyotan tells Yugi that a king's rule rests on ministers like him.

reading: The verse names Salankayan's sister, a woman with a crescent brow, spear-sharp eyes and fine teeth, called Aappi, as one of the brides; the grammar runs into the next verse.
nuance: The sentence is not complete until verse 219, and her name is not certain.
event: Salankayan's sister is named as one of the brides to be given to Yugi.

reading: The king gives Yugi in marriage Tilakasenai, sister of Paratakan, praised through the land, together with Salankayan's sister, in a wedding the wide earth hears of.
event: Pradyotan gives two brides to Yugi in marriage.

reading: The king bids him go and walk the old city first and sends him off; the many people praise and bow, and Yugi goes and sees his king.
event: Pradyotan lets Yugi go, and Yugi returns to Udayanan.

tamil: வத்தவ குமரன் பாதம் வந்தனை செய்த மைச்சன்
இத்தல முழுது மாளு மினியநன் மாமன் சொன்ன
ஒத்தநன் மொழியைக் கேட்டே யுவந்துட னிருந்த போழ்தில்
சித்திரப் பாவை மார்கள் செல்வனை வணங்கிச் சொல்வார்.
reading: Yugi bows to the prince's feet and tells him his uncle's fitting words, and as the king sits glad the picture-like ladies bow before him and are about to speak.
nuance: The e-text prints this verse without its number.
event: Yugi reports Pradyotan's words to Udayanan, and the court ladies come to him.

tamil: பந்தடி காண்க வென்னப் பார்த்திப னினிய னாகிக்
கந்துகப் பூசல் காணக் கலிற்றின்மீ தேறி வந்து
கொந்தலர் மாலை மாதர் குழுவுடன் சூழ நிற்ப
வந்தனள் பதுமை தோழி வனப்பிரா சனையென் பாளாம்.
reading: The king, glad, mounts an elephant to watch the ball-play and the ball contest while the ladies stand round him, and Vanapirasanai, Padumai's friend, comes.
event: Udayanan watches ball-play, and Vanapirasanai arrives.

tamil: ஓரேழு பந்து கொண்டே யொன்றென்றி னெற்றிச் செல்லப்
பாரெழு துகளு மாடப் பலகல னொலிப்ப வாடிச்
காரெழு குழலி நல்ல காஞ்சன மாலை வந்தாள்.
reading: She keeps seven balls going, each thrown up in turn, while dust rises, ornaments ring and her thousand strokes end; then Kanchanamalai, dark of hair, comes.
nuance: Line 3 is hard, and it is not sure whether she or her hands stop the play before Kanchanamalai steps in.
event: Vanapirasanai plays with seven balls, and Kanchanamalai arrives to take her turn.

title: வத்தவ காண்டம் 224-241 (3/3)
theme: At the end of Vatsa kandam a ball-play contest is won by Mananigai after Dattai's side is beaten; the king marries her, Dattai's anger yields to worship, and he later marries Virisikai by sacrifice, ending as the husband of four chaste queens ruling in peace.
source_issues: Verse 224: the maid's name Ayirapathi is split across a word break.
Verse 229: lines 3 and 4 are heavily compounded and may be damaged.
Verse 233: line 3 is damaged (தரிவுவிச்சை).
Verse 234: line 1 is corrupt.
Verse 236: last line unclear.
Verse 231: the numeral in line 1 reads thirty-two.

cast.role: Padumai's maid who opens the ball-play
Dattai's friend
another friend of Padumai
a woman who strikes three thousand
Dattai, Vasavadatta, the king's first queen
Mananigai, daughter of the Kosala king, who wins the contest and becomes a queen
the watchers of the contest
the ladies who ride to the wedding temple
the king of Vatsa (named by titles in these verses)
the kings who bring tribute

tamil: வேய்மிகு தடக்கை தன்னால் வியந்துபந் துடனே யேந்திக்
காய்பொனின் கலன்க ளார்ப்பக் கார்மயி லாட்டம் போல
ஆயிரத் தைஞ்ஞா றேற்றி யடித்தன ளகல வப்பால்
ஆய்புகழ்ப் பதுமை தாதி யயிராப திபந்து கொண்டாள்.
reading: A maid of Padumai takes up the ball with her bamboo-slim broad hand, strikes it fifteen hundred times with her ornaments ringing like a peacock dancing in the rain cloud, and steps back.
nuance: The maid's name is written across a word break in line 4; the verse opens a ball-play contest whose two sides are only implied.
event: Padumai's maid takes the ball, strikes it fifteen hundred times and then withdraws.

tamil: சீரேறு மிமில்போற் கொண்டைச் சில்வண்டுந் தேனும் பாடப்
பாரோர்க ளினிது நோக்கும் பல்கலஞ் சிலம்போ டார்ப்ப
ஈராயி ரங்கை யேற்றி யிருகரத் தடித்து விட்டாள்
தோராத வழகி தத்தை தோழி விசுவ லேகை வந்தாள்.
reading: Dattai's friend Visuvalekai comes forward and strikes the ball two thousand times with both hands, her ornaments and anklets sounding.
event: Visuvalekai, Dattai's friend, strikes the ball two thousand times with both hands.

tamil: கருங்குழ னெடுவேற் கண்ணாள் காரிகை பந்தெ டுத்துப்
பெருங்கல னினிதி னார்ப்பப் பெய்வளை கலக லென்ன
ஒருங்குமுன் கையின் மீதி லோரைஞ்ஞூ றடித்து விட்டாள்
கருங்கணி பதுமை தோழி காரிகை யொருத்தி வந்தாள்
reading: Another friend of Padumai, a woman of dark long hair and spear-like eyes, takes the ball and strikes it five hundred times along her forearm to the clash of her bangles.
event: A friend of Padumai strikes the ball five hundred times along her forearm.

tamil: ஆரியை யென்னு நாம வரிவைகைக் கொண்டு பந்தைச்
சேரமின் சிலம்பு மார்ப்பச் சிறுநுதன் முத்த ரும்பச்
சீரின்மூ வாயி ரங்கை சிறந்தவ ளடித்த பின்பு
பேரிசைத் தத்தை யாயம் பெருங்குழாத் தினிதி னோக்காள்.
reading: A woman named Ariyai takes the ball and strikes it three thousand times, and after that the company of Dattai no longer looks at the gathering with pleasure.
nuance: The verse does not say which side Ariyai plays for; the loss of heart in Dattai's company in the last line suggests she is of the other side.
event: Ariyai strikes the ball three thousand times, and Dattai's company loses heart.

tamil: அருவரு மேற்பா ரின்றி யோர்ந்தவ ணெஞ்சங் கூர்ந்து
திருநுதன் மாது நொந்து சிறப்பின்றி யிருந்த போழ்தின்
மருவுகோ சலத்து மன்னன் மகளுரு வரிவை நாமம்
சுரிகுழன் மான னீகை சொலற்கருங் கற்பி னாளே.
reading: With no one left to answer the score, Dattai sits troubled and joyless; the verse then names a new woman, Mananigai, the daughter of the king of Kosala, of unspeakable chastity.
nuance: Mananigai is introduced as the daughter of the king of Kosala and praised for her chastity before she does anything, so the poem marks her virtue first and her skill second.
event: Dattai sits dejected, and Mananigai, the Kosala king's daughter, is introduced.

tamil: இளம்பிறை நுதல்வேற் கண்ணி யினியவிற் புருவ வேய்த்தோள்
இளங்கிளி மொழிநற் கொங்கை யீடில்பொற் கலச மல்குல்
இளமணிப் படம்பொன் வாழை யிருகுறங் காலம் பண்டி
இளம்புற வடிக ளாமை யிடைமின் பூங் குழலி னாளே.
reading: The poet describes Mananigai limb by limb, from forehead like a young moon to waist, thighs and feet, with images of the bamboo, the parrot, the golden pot and the plantain.
nuance: Line 3 and 4 images are heavy with rare words and may be damaged; the order of the limbs is only partly clear.

tamil: ஆங்கொரு கார ணத்திற் றத்தைபால் வந்தி ருந்தாள்
பூங்கொடி தோல்வி கண்டு பொறுப்பிலா மனத்த ளாகித்
தீங்குறு தத்தை தன்னைச் சீருடன் வணங்கிப் போந்து
பாங்குறு மிலக்க ணங்கள் பந்தடி பலவுஞ் சொன்னாள்.
reading: Mananigai, who has come to Dattai on some business, cannot bear to see her defeated, bows to her with respect and tells her the rules of ball-play of many kinds.
nuance: The verse says she came for another reason and does not name it; her instruction of Dattai, not her own play, answers the defeat.
event: Mananigai bows to the defeated Dattai and tells her the rules of ball-play.

reading: Taking a large ball, Mananigai strikes it with both hands in turn, sends it running, hides it in the garland, and plays it like a snake that has just given birth, bowing and rising as she plays.
nuance: Line 3 is hard: the gloss of the ball hidden in a garland and of the snake dance is mine; the numeral in line 1 reads as thirty-two.
event: Mananigai plays the ball with both hands, running it, hiding it in the garland and making it dance.

reading: Mananigai plays on, dancing the round and standing dances while the sweat on her brow is wiped on her silk and her slender waist bends.
event: Mananigai keeps up the dance-steps of ball-play, sweating and bending at the waist.

reading: All who watch are amazed, saying they have never seen the like, and ask whether she is a woman of the sky, a goddess of the lesser order, a woman of the nether world or a vidyadhara, and that there is none like her on earth.
nuance: Line 3 is damaged (தரிவுவிச்சை), and the classes named are read as a goddess of the vyantara order and a woman of the bhavana world.
event: The onlookers wonder at Mananigai and ask whether she is a divine woman.

reading: When she takes up the ball on her fingertips and strikes it, her bangles ring and the balls rise through sky and earth like whirlwinds.
nuance: Line 1 is corrupt (காந்தணன் ஒருமுன் கைக் கன்னியன்); only the ringing bangles and the whirlwind simile are clear.
event: Mananigai strikes the ball so that it rises through sky and earth to the sound of her bangles.

reading: As the woman strikes the ball ten times, her anklets and small bells ring, the pearl strands sway on her young breasts, and bees and honey-gatherers hum above her hair.
event: Mananigai strikes ten, her ornaments ringing and bees gathering about her hair.

reading: The sound of her anklets and bracelets is sweeter than any music or the songs of the gods, and wins the king's heart.
nuance: The last line is unclear (கூடகமனத்தினற்கு மரனினிய னாயினன்); I read only that the king is won and turns kind.
event: The sound of Mananigai's ornaments wins the king's heart.

reading: Saying that, rising and falling, there is none but she in all the world who plays so before ladies and a king, she strikes the ball eight thousand times with her forehead-hand.
nuance: The count is the highest of the contest and beats Ariyai's three thousand in verse 227 by a wide margin; line 2 on the king and women is not clear.
event: Mananigai strikes the ball eight thousand times, exceeding every earlier score.

tamil: பிடிமிசை மாதர் போந்து பெருமணக் கோயில் புக்கார்
கடிமலர்க் கோதை மன்னன் காவிநன் விழிமா னீகை
இடிமின்னி னுசுப்பி னாளை யின்புறப் புணர்ந்தி ருப்பத்
துடியிடைத் தத்தை கேட்டுத் தோற்றிய சீற்றத் தானாள்.
reading: The women ride a she-elephant to the great wedding temple, where the king takes the dark-eyed Mananigai in joy, and Dattai hears of it and is seized with anger.
nuance: The verse turns the contest into a courtship: the king reaches Mananigai through the skill she showed. Dattai's anger is her first response to the second queen.
event: The party rides to the wedding temple, the king unites with Mananigai, and Dattai hears and grows angry.

tamil: துன்னிரு ணீங்கிக் காலை தூமலர் கொண்டு தத்தை
மன்னவ னடிவ ணங்க மனமகிழ் வின்றி நின்ற
அன்னமென் னடையி னாளை யகமகிழ் குளிரக் கூறி
மன்னன்மா னீகை தன்னை மணமிகச் செய்து கொண்டான்.
reading: At dawn Dattai brings flowers and worships the king's feet while Mananigai stands joyless; the king speaks to her to comfort her, and then marries her with full rites.
nuance: The speech of consolation is only reported, and the verse does not say what the king told her. Dattai's worship follows her anger of verse 238 with no word on how it was resolved.
event: Dattai worships the king with flowers; he comforts Mananigai and marries her fully.

tamil: தேவியர் மூவர் கூடத் தேர்மன்னன் சேர்ந்து சென்னாட்
பூவின்மஞ் சரியைப் போலும் பொற்புநல் விரிசி கையைத்
தாவில்சீர் வேள்வி தன்னாற் றரணீசன் மணந்தா னன்றே.
reading: With the three queens present the king marries Virisikai, like a bunch of flowers set among the garland, by a proper fire sacrifice.
nuance: The marriage is by vedic sacrifice (வேள்வி), as the verse names it; the work does not comment on that rite in a Jain epic.
event: The king marries Virisikai in the presence of his three queens, by sacrifice.

tamil: நட்புடைக் கற்பு மாதர் நால்வரு மன்ன னுள்ளத்
துட்புடை யிருப்ப நாளு மொருகுறை வின்றித் துய்த்துத்
திட்புடை மன்னர் வந்து திறையளந் தடிவ ணங்க
நட்புடை நாட்டை யெல்லா நரபதி யாண்டு சென்றான்.
reading: The four chaste women keep a place in the king's heart and he enjoys them without lack, while firm kings come to pay tribute and bow at his feet, and the king rules all his friendly land.
nuance: The picture of an enjoying, tribute-taking king closes the chapter with no sign of the renunciation that the epic's own tradition would later expect.
event: The king lives happily with his four wives and rules while other kings bring tribute.

title: நரவாகன காண்டம் 242-262 (1/3)
theme: The king flies with the queen in the sky chariot the god's mantra supplies; Naravahanan is born and grows up with four companions, sees and unites with Madanamanjikai, who is carried off by the Vidyadhara Manasavegan, and Manasavegan's sister Vegavati, sent to break her firmness, falls in desire for the prince and takes Madanamanjikai's form.
source_issues: Verse 244 line 1: whether Urumannuva speaks or is bidden to speak is not clear.
Verse 249 lines 1 to 2: the grammar is hard and the speaker of the mantra is not named.
Verse 251 lines 1 and 4: stray full stops inside words (கிரி.யும், புரி.ய).
Verse 253 lines 3 to 4: the four names run together.
Verse 254 line 4 and verse 255 lines 1 to 2: hard to read.
Verse 260 lines 1 to 2: the speaker and the one addressed are not clear.

cast.role: the king of Vatsa, whose queen is with child
Udayanan's queen (called தத்தை in these verses), who longs to travel the sky
the god who once showed Udayanan water and gave him a mantra to call him
Udayanan's minister, who recalls the god
the skilled folk and common people who bow to the king
the king, queen and friends riding the sky chariot
Udayanan's friends who ride with him
the son born to Udayanan and Vasavadatta
a minister's son, companion of Naravahanan
a minister's son, companion of Naravahanan
a minister's son, companion of Naravahanan
a minister's son, companion of Naravahanan
the four minister's sons who grow up with the prince
the girl, born of Kalinga Senai, whom Naravahanan sees at ball-play
the Vidyadhara king who carries her off to the silver mountain
Manasavegan's younger sister, sent to break Madanamanjikai's firmness

tamil: எத்திக்கு மடிப்ப டுத்தி யெழில்பெறச் செங்கோல் செல்லும்
பெற்றிசெய் வேந்தன் றன்னைப் பெருமைவேற் றானை மன்னை
வித்தைசெய் சனங்கண் மாந்தர் வியந்தடி வணங்க மின்னும்
முற்றிழை மாலைத் தத்தை முனிவில்சீர் மயற்கை யானாள்.
reading: Because the king's sceptre runs justly over every quarter, skilled folk and common men bow to his feet, and Dattai, the queen in her garland, falls into a longing.
nuance: The word மயற்கை (longing, bewilderment) opens the next verse, where the longing is named as a wish to fly.
event: People marvel and bow at the just king's feet, and the queen Dattai falls into a longing.

tamil: நிறைபுகழ் வனப்பு நங்கை நிலவிய வுதரந் தன்னுட்
பிறையென வளரச் செல்வன் பேதையும் விசும்பிற் செல்லும்
குறைபெறு வேட்கை கேட்ட கொற்றவன் மனத்தி னெண்ணி
அறைபுக ழமைச்சர் தம்மை யழைத்தனன் வினவி னானே.
reading: As the child grows in the queen's womb like a crescent, she is seized by a lack in her longing, to go in the sky; the king hears it, thinks it over and calls his ministers to ask.
event: The queen in pregnancy longs to travel the sky, and the king calls his ministers to ask what can be done.

tamil: உருமண்ணுவா விதனைச் செப்பு முன்னொரு தினத்தின் வேட்டைப்
பெருமலை வனத்தி னீரின் வேட்கையாற் பிறந்த துன்பம்
மருவுறு வருத்தங் கண்டோர் வானவன் வந்து தோன்றிப்
reading: Urumannuva recalls to the king that once, when thirst overcame him on a hunt in the great hill forest, a god appeared and showed him water and ended his great distress.
nuance: Line 1 can be read as the king bidding Urumannuva speak, or as Urumannuva beginning; the sense of the recalled rescue is the same.
event: Urumannuva reminds the king how a god once appeared to the thirsty king in a hunt and showed him water.

tamil: இன்னமோ ரிடர்வந் தாலு மென்னைநீர் நினைக்க வென்று
மன்னுமோர் மந்தி ரந்தான் வண்மையி னளித்துப் போந்தான்
சொன்னமா மந்தி ரத்தைச் சூழ்ச்சியி னினைக்க வென்றான்
பின்னவ னினைத்த போழ்தே பீடுடை யமரன் வந்தான்.
reading: The god, when he left, gave a lasting mantra and said to think of it in any trouble; the king now thinks of it with care and the proud god arrives at once.
event: Udayanan calls to mind the mantra the god gave him, and the god comes.

tamil: பலவுப சாரஞ் சொல்லப் பார்மன்னற் கிதனைச் செப்பும்
நலிவுசெய் சிறையிற் பட்ட நாளிலுஞ் சவரர் சுற்றி
வலியவந் தலைத்த போதும் வாசவ தத்தை நின்னைச்
சிலதினம் பிரிந்த போதுஞ் செற்றோரைச் செகுத்த போதும்.
reading: After many courtesies the god speaks to the king: in the days of prison, when the savaras closed in and harassed him, when he was parted from Vasavadatta, and when he killed his enemies...
nuance: The sentence is left unfinished here and is completed in the next verse: in none of these troubles did the king call on him.
event: The god begins to list the king's past dangers, prison, the savara attack, the parting from Vasavadatta and his killing of foes.

tamil: மித்திர னென்றே யென்னை வேண்டிமுன் னினைத்தா யில்லை
பொற்றிரு மார்ப விந்நாட் புதுமையி னினைத்த தென்னை
உத்தரஞ் சொல்க வென்ன வொளியுமி ழமரன் கேட்கச்
சித்திரப் பாவை வானிற் செலவினை வேட்டா ளென்றான்.
reading: The god says the king never once thought of him as a friend in those troubles and asks why he has remembered him on this strange day; the king answers that the queen has wished to go in the sky.
nuance: Lines 1 to 3 are the god's question and line 4 is the king's answer, given by the narrator in indirect speech. The god treats the bond as one that needs a call.
event: The god asks why the king calls on him now, and the king answers that the queen longs to travel the sky.

tamil: எங்களிற் கரும மாக்கு மியல்புள் தீர்த்துக் கொண்டோம்
திங்களின் முகத்திற் பாவை செலவுநின் னாலே யன்றி
நன்கினி யமரன் கேட்டு நரபதி கேளி தென்றான்.
reading: The king explains that what they could do among themselves they have done, but the queen's travel in the sky cannot come about except through the god, and so he thought of him now; the god hears it well and tells the king to listen.
event: Udayanan tells the god why he called him, and the god bids him listen.

tamil: வெள்ளிய மலையிற் றேவன் விரைக் குழலாள் வயிற்றின்
உள்ளவின் பத்தி னாலே வுலவுவான் சிந்தை யானாள்
கள்ளவிழ் மாலை வேந்தன் கதிர்மணித் தேரி னேறிப்
புள்ளெனப் பறக்க மந்த்ர மீதெனக் கொடுத்துப் போந்தான்.
reading: The god tells the king of a god of the silver mountain who has come to dwell in the fragrant-haired woman's womb, whose delight makes her wander in thought; the king then mounts the jewelled chariot, and the mantra is given for flying like a bird.
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are hard to read, and who gives the mantra in lines 3 to 4 is inferred from the story, since no one is named; the verse seems to trace the longing to the being in her womb.
event: The god explains the cause of the queen's longing and gives the king a mantra to make the chariot fly.

tamil: வெற்றித்தே ரேறி வென்வேல் வேந்தனுந் தேவி தானும்
மற்றுநற் றோழன் மாரும் வரிசையி னேறி வானம்
உற்றந்த வழிய தேகி யுத்தர திக்கி னின்ற
பெற்றிநல் லிமயங் கண்டு பேர்ந்துகீழ்த் திசையுஞ் சென்றான்.
reading: The king and queen and their friends mount the victory chariot in order, rise into the sky, see the Himalaya in the north and then turn to the east.
event: Udayanan, the queen and friends fly the chariot north to the Himalaya and then east.

tamil: உதயநற் கிரி.யும் கண்டே யுற்றுடன் றெற்திற் சென்று
பொதியமா மலையும் காணாப் பொருவில்சீர்க் குடபா னின்ற
மதிகதி ரவியு மத்த வான்கிரி கண்டு மீண்டும்
இதமுள தேசம் பார்த்தே யினியதம் புரி.ய டைந்தார்.
reading: They see the eastern hill of sunrise, go on to the south and the Podiyil hill, see the western mountain where sun and moon set, and having seen the good lands return to their pleasant city.
nuance: Lines 1 and 4 carry stray full stops inside words in the edition (கிரி.யும், புரி.ய).
event: The riders fly over the eastern, southern and western hills and return to their city.

tamil: மாதுதன் வயாநோய் தீர்ந்து வளநகர் புக்க பின்பு
தீதின்றிக் கோள்க ளெல்லாஞ் சிறந்துநல் வழியை நோக்கப்
போதினற் குமரன் றேன்றப் புரவல னினிய னாகிச்
சோதிப்பொன் னறைதி றந்து தூவினன் சனங்கட் கெல்லாம்.
reading: When the queen's longing has ended and they have entered the rich city, the planets all stand well, the prince is born, and the king, glad, opens the gold chamber and scatters wealth to all the people.
event: The prince is born under good planets, and the king opens his gold chamber and gives to all.

tamil: நரவாக னன்னே யென்று நரபதி நாமஞ் செய்தான்
விரிவாகு மதிய மைச்சர் மிக்கநாற் குமரர் பேர்தாம்
பரிவார்கோ முகனும் பாங்காந் தரிசக னாக தத்தன்
குரவம்பூ மேனி யான குலமறி பூதி யாமே.
reading: The king names the child Naravahanan, and the four sons of his ministers have the names Gomukhan, Tarisakan, Nagadattan and Bhuti.
nuance: The line that gives the four names runs together across lines 3 and 4 (பாங்காந் தரிசக னாக தத்தன், குலமறி பூதி), so the exact form of the names is somewhat uncertain.
event: Udayanan names his son Naravahanan, and the four minister's sons are named.

tamil: நால்வருந் துணைவ ராகி நறுநெய்பா லுடன ருந்தி
பான்மரத் தொட்டி லிட்டுப் பரவியுந் தவழ்ந்து மூன்றாம்
மால்பிறை போல்வ ளர்ந்து வரிசையி னிளமை நீங்கிப்
பான்மொழி வாணி தன்னைப் பாங்கினிற் சேர்த்தா ரன்றே.
reading: The four become his companions, share his ghee and milk, crawl in the wooden cradle and grow like the third-day moon; when childhood is past, they place him in the company of Vani.
nuance: Who is placed and who places him is not stated; பான்மொழி வாணி may be the goddess of learning or a teacher's name.
event: The prince and the four minister's sons grow up together and are placed with Vani for learning.

tamil: ஞானநற் குமரி தன்னை நலமுழு துண்டு மாரன்
மானவிற் கணைக்கி லக்கா மன்மத னென்னக் கண்டோர்
வானவக் குமரர் போல வாரண மேறித் தோழர்
சேனைமுன் பின்னுஞ் செல்லச் சீர்நகர் வீதி சென்றான்.
reading: The youth, who has taken all the sweetness of learning, looks to onlookers like Kama himself, and with his friends and army before and behind rides an elephant through the town's streets.
nuance: Line 1 is hard: ஞானநற் குமரி is read here as learning personified, but that is not certain, and line 2 is hard to parse.
event: Naravahanan, grown and learned, rides an elephant through the streets with his friends and army.

tamil: ஒளிர்குழற் கலிங்க சேனை யுதர்த்தி னுற்ப வித்த
வளிநறும் பூஞ்சு கந்த மதனமஞ் சிகைதன் மேனி
குளிரிளந் தென்றல் வீசக் கோலமுற் றத்துப் பந்தைக்
களிகயற் கண்ணி யாடக் காவல குமரன் கண்டான்.
reading: As a cool breeze blows on Madanamanjikai, born of Kalingasenai, who plays with the ball in the decorated court, the king's son sees her.
event: Naravahanan sees Madanamanjikai playing ball in the court.

tamil: மட்டவிழ் கோதை தன்னை மன்னவ குமரன் கண்டு
இட்டநன் மார னம்பா லிருவரு மயக்க முற்று
மட்டவிழ் மலர்ச்சோ லைக்குள் மன்னவ குமரன் மின்னின்
இட்டிடை மாதைத் தந்தே யின்புறப் புணர்ந்தா னன்றே.
reading: The prince sees the garlanded girl and both are bewildered by the god of love's arrow; in the flower grove he unites with the slender-waisted girl at once, to their joy.
nuance: The verse names no wedding, no go-between and no family: sight and union come together. Whether there is a rite that is left out is not clear from the verse.
event: The prince and Madanamanjikai fall in love at the sight and unite in the flower grove.

tamil: இருவரும் போகந் துய்த்தே யிளைத்துயில் கொள்ளும் போழ்து
மருவிய விச்சை மன்னன் மானச வேக னென்பான்
திருநிற மாதைக் கண்டு திறத்தினிற் கொண்டு சென்று
பெருவரை வெள்ளி மீதிற் பீடுறு புரம்புக் கானே.
reading: While the two sleep after their pleasure, the Vidyadhara king Manasavegan sees the radiant girl, takes her by his skill and enters his city on the silver mountain.
nuance: The abduction falls at the moment of rest after union, so the girl is taken before the lovers are fully known to the household.
event: Manasavegan carries off the sleeping Madanamanjikai to the silver mountain.

tamil: தன்னுடை நோயு ரைக்கத் தையலு மோனங் கொண்டே
இன்னுயிர்க் கணவன் றன்னை இனிமையி னினைத்தி ருப்ப
மின்னிடைத் தங்கை யான வேகநல் வதியை யேவி
மன்னிய நிறை யழிக்க வாஞ்சையின் விடுத்தா னன்றே.
reading: When Manasavegan tells her his pain she keeps silent and holds her husband sweetly in mind; so he sends his slender-waisted sister Vegavati, to ruin the firmness she keeps.
nuance: Silence and remembering her husband are the whole of her defence; the verse calls her husband இன்னுயிர்க் கணவன், though no rite of marriage was told in the last verses.
event: Manasavegan woos her in vain, and sends Vegavati to break her steadfastness.

tamil: அன்புற வவளுஞ் சொல்ல வசலித மனத்த ளாகி
இன்புறுந் தன்னோர் நாத னிந்திரன் போலு மென்னப்
பண்புணர் மொழியைக் கேட்டுப் பரவச மனத்த ளாகி
நண்பொடு விசும்பின் வந்து நரவாக னனைக்கண் டாளே.
reading: Madanamanjikai, unmoved, says with love that her lord is like Indra himself; hearing the words of such a virtuous woman, Vegavati falls into a trance of feeling and comes out in the sky, and sees Naravahanan.
nuance: Who says what in lines 1 and 2 is hard to fix; the speech is taken here to be Madanamanjikai's, praising her husband, and Vegavati's trance is taken to follow from it.
event: Madanamanjikai praises her lord to Vegavati, who comes to the sky and sees Naravahanan.

tamil: கண்டபின் காமங் கூர்ந்து கார்விசும் பதனி னிற்பப்
புண்டவழ் வேலிற் காளை பூங்குழ லாட்கி ரங்கி
வண்டலர் சோலை மாடம் வனமெங்குந் தேடு கின்றான்
தொண்டைவா யுடைய வேக வதியுஞ்சூ தினிலே வந்தாள்.
reading: On seeing him Vegavati's desire grows and she stands in the dark sky, while the youth, stricken, searches the groves, the towers and the whole wood for the girl, and Vegavati comes down by guile.
nuance: The desire in line 1 is taken as Vegavati's, since she is the one who has just seen him, but the grammar does not fix it.
event: Vegavati, desiring Naravahanan, descends by a trick while he is searching everywhere for Madanamanjikai.

reading: Vegavati takes the shape of Madanamanjikai, doe-eyed, with a moon-like face, wearing the pleasing disguise with delight, and sits in a bower within the thicket.
event: Vegavati takes on Madanamanjikai's form and waits in a thicket pavilion.

title: நரவாகன காண்டம் 263-282 (2/3)
theme: The youth who joins a Vidyadhara woman is seized by her brother and dropped in the forest, where a sage rescues him and foretells his rule and marriage; he visits his parents, flies to Sridharaloka and meets a Vidyadhara who tells of a king's daughter whose dream a sage reads as a sign of his coming.
source_issues: Verses 263 to 282 are heavily corrupt in the edition: the line 'மாத விப்பொதும் பின்மயிற் றோகைபோல்' (263) and the word divisions of 268, 269 and 278 to 280 do not parse cleanly, so the speakers and the person of the sage are partly inferred.
The sage called the father of the Vatsa king (268) and the sage Sumitra (281) may be one person; the verses do not say.

cast.role: Udayanan's son, called by titles such as காளை in these verses
the Vidyadhara brother of the woman, who seizes the pair
the Vidyadhara woman who joins the youth and gives up her art
the sage who foretells the youth's rule and later reads the dream
the youth's mother, whose grief he soothes (not named in 274)
the young Vidyadhara who worships the youth's feet and names Gandharvapuram
the Vidyadhara king of Gandharvapuram, father of Nagadattai
Nilavekan's daughter who has the dream

reading: Pollen drifts down over the earth like a peacock's tail spread in the cloud-dark hour, and the proud youth, seeing the girl, finds the way clear of fault and joins with her.
nuance: The first two lines are a scene-setting image whose syntax is broken in the edition (மாத விப்பொதும்); the girl is not named, and she may be the Vidyadhara woman of the next verses.
event: The youth, having judged that no fault bars it, unites with the girl.

tamil: பூங்கு ழா அல் நீ புதியைமற் றியாரெனப்
reading: On another day the lord sees the flower-haired woman asleep and, as she comes to his side, she speaks to him at length, asking who he is, a stranger.
nuance: The verse does not say who is asleep and who speaks; it is read here as the maiden coming to the youth, though the sleeper may be the youth's own bride.
event: A woman asks the youth who he is and talks with him at length.

reading: The generous youth asks the woman to show him the form she likes best; she does, and he joins with her while Mara's arrows urge him on.
nuance: The shape-showing implies she is a Vidyadhara who can change form; the verse does not say so.
event: The woman shows the shape he asked for, and the youth joins with her.

reading: Manasavegan, master of the Vidyadhara arts, cannot find his sister, learns from the court that she has gone, comes in anger and seizes both.
nuance: His anger is the wronged brother's: the verse treats the pair's union as an offence to be punished, with no word for the woman's own will.
event: Manasavegan learns his sister has left and seizes her and the youth.

reading: Manasavegan leaves the youth in the sky and goes down; the woman of the dark hair gives up her Vidyadhara art, and the youth falls into the forest.
nuance: The verse does not say why the youth falls, whether her art held him up or the brother let go; the readings turn on the doubtful wording of line 2.
event: Manasavegan abandons the youth in mid-air, his sister drops her art, and the youth falls into the forest.

reading: As the fallen youth lies like a leaf of bamboo, the great sage, the beloved father of the bright-speared king of Vatsa, who is to cast off future births, sees him.
nuance: The sage is called the father of the Vatsa king; the verse does not say he is the same as the Sumitra of verse 281, and an earlier life of the king is possible.
event: The sage sees the fallen youth.

reading: Knowing by his power of enlightenment what has happened, the sage goes out in love, names the youth and his father, and the youth comes and bows.
nuance: போதி (line 1) is read as the sage's wisdom or insight; the word is rare in this sense.
event: The sage says the youth's name and his father's name, and the youth bows to him.

reading: The youth asks the sage how he knows his father and himself, and the sage, in due order, tells who they are; the youth listens with deepening feeling and then hears one thing more.
event: The youth asks how the sage knew them; the sage explains.

reading: The sage says the sages' word is that he will conquer and rule the Vidyadhara cities and that his state is unfailing; the great ascetic tells it truly.
event: The sage foretells that the youth will rule the Vidyadhara cities.

reading: The sage tells him the whole realm on the silver mountain will come under his feet with wealth beyond reproach, and the youth listens.
event: The sage promises the youth the Vidyadhara realm of Vellimalai.

reading: The youth leaves the great ascetic, goes to the city, and after seeing his father and mother, tells them lovingly how his misfortune ended and his beloved was parted from him.
nuance: The speaker of the last line is called அன்னோன் ('that one'); the verse names no wife, so the beloved's parting is either from the Vidyadhara woman or from his wedded wife.
event: The youth rejoins his parents and tells them of the end of his trouble and of his parted wife.

reading: He soothes his mother's grief by reporting what the true ascetic said, mounts the sky-going chariot, and goes happily.
event: The youth tells his mother what the ascetic said, ends her grief, and mounts a sky-chariot.

reading: With love the chariot goes along the sky-road southwards to Sridharaloka on the Vidyadhara ridge, and the youth, told to rest by a fair pond, stays gladly.
event: The youth flies south to Sridharaloka and rests by a pond.

reading: He stands at the long bank, bathes without shaking, anoints himself with fragrant water and sits there; a young man seeing his feet worships them.
event: The youth bathes and sits at the pond, and a young man worships his feet.

reading: The lord asks the young man who he is, and the cool-tongued Vidyadhara says his city is Gandharvapuram on the hard-to-reach hill.
event: The youth asks the stranger who he is; the stranger names Gandharvapuram.

reading: The Vidyadhara king Nilavekan has a fair daughter, Nagadattai of fame, and the flower-vine Manmatha-vilasai, as another daughter.
nuance: Whether Nagadattai and Anangavilasai are two daughters or one woman with two names cannot be fixed from the fragmentary syntax of lines 3 and 4.
event: The stranger names the king's daughters Nagadattai and Anangavilasai.

reading: Asleep on a bed with bee-sung garlands, the sweet-voiced girl dreams that a curse of power, lion and fish, rose from the earth in her lover's company.
nuance: The dream is told in bare images (சிங்கம், மீன், சாபம்) whose referents the verse does not give; it is the sage's reply in 282 that makes them a sign.
event: The girl dreams of a lion and a fish and a curse that rises from the earth.

reading: In the dream a creature comes down from the hill and bites the pearl necklace on her breast, then sets a fragrant garland on her with pride; the girl wakes and tells her kin.
event: The girl sees a creature take her necklace and crown her with a garland, and tells her kin.

reading: The king of the victorious spear hears, goes to the unreachable sage Sumitra, bows at his feet in due form, and asks the ascetic about the good dream.
nuance: The sage here is named சுமித்திர, and the Vidyadhara king consults him like the youth's own guide of verse 268; whether they are one person is left open.
event: The king hears the dream, goes to the sage Sumitra and asks him to read it.

reading: The sage, who has understood, gives grace and says the beloved lord now arriving will wed the king's daughter and, with the disc complete, will rule this earth.
event: The sage reads the dream and says the coming youth will marry the king's daughter and rule the earth.

title: நரவாகன காண்டம் 283-302 (3/3)
theme: The Vidyadhara king gives the youth his daughter at an open gathering of kings, after which the youth gains the wheel and nine treasures through Indra's grace, subdues the Vidyadhara lords, returns with his queens to his father's city, installs a son and is sent off by his father to Indra's city.
source_issues: Verse 288 line 4 breaks off in a hanging phrase about Manasavegan's mind.
Verse 289: whether 'நாக நீள்புரம்' is a city of Nagas or a serpent-named city is not settled.
Verse 291 line 4: the count 'இரண்டொன்ற ஆயிரம்' is obscure.
Verse 294 has no finite verb and runs into 295.
Verse 301 line 2 reads 'றந்த தான்', which looks damaged.
Verse 302 line 2: 'வாமன்' is not clearly the worshipped deity or its rite.
The Vidyadhara king's name, Neelavegan, comes from verse 278 of the earlier chapter; verses 283-302 call him only 'the king'.

cast.role: Udayanan's son, called the youth (காளை) and the lord of the wheel; a name not written in these verses
the Vidyadhara king whose daughter weds the youth; named in verse 278 of the earlier chapter, here called only the king
the ministers of the Vidyadhara king
the king's daughter who garlands the youth (Nagadattai in verse 278, unnamed here)
the young women of the city who gaze at the hero
Indra, who gives the treasures and the chariot
the garlanded beings of the mountain who bow to the hero
the Vidyadhara lords he subdues
the hero's queens, among them Madanamanjikai, Vegavati and Anangavilasai
the king of Vatsa, here the father (வேலரசன்)
Padumai's son

reading: The king takes in the sage's word, weighs it, and sends word to the young man that he has seen him and that he should come.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 do not say who is addressed or who carries the message; the reading takes it as the summons to the groom the sage had foretold.
event: The king, having heard the sage, sends word summoning the youth.

reading: The youth goes, taking his merit as his only wealth, meets the king face to face, and arrives gladly with the king's attendants.
nuance: Line 1 puts the youth's journey in terms of merit (புண்ணியன்), the same quality that later verses give as the cause of his rise.
event: The youth goes to the king, who receives him with joy and attendants.

reading: The king, glad, speaks sweet words of the youth, who is like Kaman without his sugarcane bow and has every fine mark, and then asks his ministers for counsel.
event: The king praises the youth and consults his ministers about giving him his daughter.

reading: The ministers, glad, warn that giving the bride to him alone would bring the other kings in anger, and so they send out word to the gathered kin and kings.
nuance: Line 4 is hard to parse; the reading takes the sending out of word as summoning the kings so the match is not a private one.
event: The ministers advise an open gathering of kings, and word is sent.

reading: With the kings gathered, the swan-gaited bride, like nectar, deftly lifts a garland bright as lightning and puts it on the young man named earlier.
nuance: The bride chooses; the garland is hers to give, in front of the kings the ministers wanted present.
event: At the gathering of kings the bride garlands the youth.

reading: The king's grand sacrificial fire sets the wedding, and the pair delight in each other, while Manasavegan's mind is said to be afraid.
nuance: Line 4 breaks off in a hanging phrase about Manasavegan's mind, which verse 289 does not finish, so what he fears is left unstated.
event: The wedding is held at the fire and the couple unite.

reading: The hero mounts a swift elephant and appears in the middle of the long city of the Nagas, and the young women drink him in with their lotus eyes as though he were Kaman.
nuance: 'நாக நீள்புரம்' could be a city of Nagas or a serpent-named place; the Tamil does not settle which, and the closing 'நாள்' hangs into verse 290.
event: The hero rides the elephant into the city and the women gaze at him.

reading: The lord, who has set his mind on ruling by the wheel, goes to the mountain of the Vama Nagas, where those who see him are shown the wheel and the nine treasures.
nuance: The line ends in a list (the wheel, then nine treasures), and who gives them is not stated until the next verse names Indra's grace.
event: The hero goes to the Nagas' mountain, where the wheel and the nine treasures are seen.

reading: By Indra's gracious word the treasures are given to Kaman, and the garlanded beings of the mountain bow before him, in a number the verse gives obscurely.
nuance: Line 4, 'தோமினால் இரண்டொன்ற ஆயிரம்', is a hard count (two joined to a thousand?) and I do not fix it. Here Kaman, as in the other verses, is the hero's byname.
event: Indra's grace gives the treasures, and the mountain's beings bow to the hero.

reading: The wheel circles to the right and bows, and the greatly meritorious hero returns and at once brings every able Vidyadhara lord under his feet.
nuance: The Tamil names him a man of great merit (புண்ணியன்) in the sentence that tells the conquest, and so makes the victory a result of merit, not only of the wheel.
event: The hero, with the wheel, subdues the Vidyadhara lords in an instant.

reading: Having won the Vidyadhara lords' tribute, he casts wealth to those who seek refuge and goes with the greatness of Indra to a city of unfailing mansions.
nuance: The verse joins conquest and giving: he accepts submission and then gives to those who take refuge.
event: The hero wins the Vidyadharas' tribute, shelters those who beg refuge and goes to a splendid city.

reading: Madanamanjikai, glad of heart, Vegavati and Anangavilasai are named among his queens, with more than eight thousand ladies besides.
nuance: The verse has no verb; it lists the queens and carries into verse 295, where the enjoyment is stated.

reading: After enjoying the pleasures of the rite and gathering good merit, he sets up a single sovereignty that grows by the fruit of what he had done.
nuance: 'வேள்வி' may mean the wedding rite or a sacrifice, and I read it as the rite of marriage and kingship; the verse does not say which.
event: The hero founds his sole sovereignty after the sacrifice and the joys it brings.

reading: With his queens, bowed to by the Vidyadharas, he leaves the cloud-ringed mountain and goes to his father, the refuge of the gods.
nuance: The verse calls the father a refuge of the gods (வானவர் தஞ்சம்), which sets the father above the son's new rank.
event: The hero and his queens leave the mountain and go to his father.

reading: The city is hung with flower garlands, festoons and flags, and the king in his flower garland goes out to meet him and looks on him with wonder.
event: The father, the king, decks the city and goes out to meet his son.

reading: The son bows to his father's and mother's feet, and the moon-faced queens come and bow to their husband's father and mother in the same way.
nuance: The queens' bow includes his father and his mother; it shows the son's rank is held beneath the household's old order.
event: The son and his queens bow to his parents.

reading: After joyous embraces they enter the house, and the lord with the wheel sits in great splendour and gladly calls his sons.
event: They embrace and enter the house, and the son calls his sons.

reading: The peerless wheel-lord sets up Gomukan, Padumai's son born of her great labour, in rule.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are loosely joined; the reading takes 'அரசு நாட்டினான்' as installing Gomukan, but whether as king or as heir is not clear.
event: The hero installs Gomukan, Padumai's son, as ruler.

reading: His father, out of unfailing love and thinking of the parting, sends him off in burning sorrow, and the lord goes as he must to Indra's city.
nuance: Line 2 is damaged ('றந்த தான்'), and I read the parting as the father's grief at letting him leave.
event: The father, grieving, lets his son go and he sets off to Indra's city.

tamil: செலவநற் குமரன் சென்று தெய்வவிந் திரனைக் கண்டு
செல்வநல் வாமன் பூசைச் சீர்கண்டு வணக்கஞ் செய்து
செல்வவிந் திரன னுப்பத் திருமணித் தேரி னேறிச்
செல்வமார் புரம்பு குந்து சிறப்பினோ டிருந்தா னன்றே.
reading: The prince goes to the god Indra, bows at the worship of the Lord, takes the jewelled chariot at Indra's leave, and returns to his own city to live in splendour.
nuance: 'வாமன் பூசை' (the worship of Vaman?) could name the deity worshipped or its rite; the Tamil does not say who he is.
event: The prince visits Indra, worships, rides a gem chariot home and settles in his city.

title: துறவுக் காண்டம் 303-324 (1/3)
theme: The Thuravu Kandam opens: Udayanan, after a life of friendship, love and conquest recalled in verse, turns to a vow and is tempted by women; the passage then breaks into an elephant's rampage in the city and the arrival of wandering Charana ascetics who preach that life is a fearful bondage.
source_issues: Verse 316 repeats verse 313 word for word (flagged duplicate).
Verses 305 to 307 are lists of items without verbs; their subjects are unnamed.
Verses 310 to 316 and 324 describe an elephant's rampage between the king's vow and the ascetics' arrival, an order that may be disturbed.
Verse 303 line 4 (திருமின் போர்மின்) is unparsed.

cast.role: the king of Vatsa who turns to a vow
the king's chaste wives
Udayanan's son
the teacher the king goes to worship; identity not given beyond the name
the women who show the king forms of desire
the elephant in rut that rampages through the city
the mahouts
the armed men who go out
the people of the city
the king of the city, probably Udayanan
the great ascetics who arrive at the grove
the Charana ascetics with the power of going through the air
the sage on a fortnightly fast
the leader of the Dharma-heroes who preaches
those who came to hear him
the birds that feed on the slain

tamil: வளங்கெழு வத்த வற்கு மன்னிய காதன் மிக்க
உளங்கெழு கற்பி னார்க ளோதிமம் போலு நீரார்
இளங்கிளி மொழியி னார்க ளினிமையி னால்வ ரோடும்
துளங்கலி றிருமின் போர்மின் தூயசொன் மடந்தை தாமும்.
reading: The verse speaks of the Vatsa king's lasting love for his wives, who are chaste in mind, swan-like, parrot-voiced and sweet of speech, but the closing words are obscure.
nuance: The last line (திருமின் போர்மின்) cannot be parsed with any confidence; the verse is read only as a portrait of the wives that opens the kandam.

tamil: மண்ணியன் மடந்தை யோடு மருவினார் மிக்க மன்னன்
புண்ணிய முன்னாட் செய்த போதந்தே யுதவி செய்ய
எண்ணிய கரும மெல்லா மியைபுட னாகப் பின்னும்
புண்ணிய நோன்பு நோற்கப் பொருந்திய மனத்த னானான்.
reading: Having lived with his queen, the king, because merit done in earlier days now lends its help and all he planned has gone well, turns his mind to taking up a vow of merit.
nuance: The renunciation is framed as the fruit of earlier merit, so the turn from the world is itself given a cause in karma; the verse does not name any birth.
event: Udayanan, his affairs prospering, resolves to take up a vow of merit.

reading: A speaking 'I' lists what his friend Yugi, his wife Vasavadatta and the child she bore had done for him.
nuance: The first person (என்றனக்கு, 'to me') shows the voice is the king's own recollection; the unit does not say it is a speech to anyone.

reading: The recollection goes on: the son is named Naravahana, the Danava land on the mountain is brought under the discus, and rival kings come to praise.
nuance: Only line 1 names Naravahana; the subjects of lines 2 to 4 are not named, and the discus is read from அங்கரண நேமி (அரண நேமி in the edition's division).
event: The son Naravahana is named; the Danavas' land is brought under the discus; kings come to praise.

reading: The recollection reaches Indra's sending and the son's reaching a high state, with the gods gathered, as the lord departs at that moment.
nuance: The subjects are unnamed and the verse is a list of items without verbs of its own, so what is sent, and who rises, is uncertain.
event: Indra's sending, the son's rise and the gods' gathering are recalled; the lord departs.

reading: Coming back to his incomparable pleasures, the king thinks they are the fruit of his earlier penance, grows weary of them and of women, and goes to see and bow at the feet of the radiant Vamana.
nuance: The thought that pleasure is the harvest of past penance becomes the reason to give pleasure up: the fruit is spent, so he seeks the penance again.
event: Udayanan, disgusted with pleasure, goes to see and worship the teacher Kanti Vamanan.

reading: As the great man's vow of merit begins, women with spear-bright eyes show him the forms of desire to feed on his mind.
nuance: The temptation arrives at the moment the vow starts, as a trial rather than a lapse.
event: Women tempt the king with forms of desire as his vow begins.

reading: The verse sets the king's crossing of the sea of delusion for loving women beside an elephant that shows its threefold rut and shakes off the fetter on its foot.
nuance: Whether the elephant is a simile for the king's shedding of his bonds or the literal start of the rampage that the next verses describe is not settled by the Tamil; the verse reads as both.
event: An elephant in rut shakes off its foot-fetter.

reading: The elephant, angry and as hot as Death, leaps on the mahouts and many people, grinds them down, and spits fire with its feet and its searching eyes.
nuance: The brief comparison to Death (காலன்) is the poem's own and no doctrine is claimed.
event: The elephant rushes on mahouts and people and crushes them.

reading: The march is described in sound: thunder-like blasts, flags and walls cracking, and tusks cutting as the going continues.
nuance: The verse is pure description; who marches and what is cut is not named.

reading: Soldiers go out as drums and big drums crash, and the townspeople shake.
event: Soldiers go out to the beat of drums while the townspeople tremble.

reading: The elephant tears open the few mahouts, wears their entrails as garlands on its tusks, and grinds the divine elephant under foot, and the hurt elephant runs.
nuance: Which elephant is the 'divine elephant' (கடவுள் யானை) and which the hurt one is not clear from the verse.
event: The elephant kills its mahouts and grinds another elephant down, then a hurt elephant runs off.

reading: The frightened townspeople go to the king and say the elephant has killed many; he tells them to go and stay in the high mansions near the water.
nuance: The king is named only by a title, so the verse does not show which king; the context points to Udayanan's own city.
event: The townspeople report the elephant's killings to the king, who tells them to take shelter on the high mansions.

reading: The verse repeats verse 313 word for word: soldiers go out, drums crash and the townspeople shake.
nuance: An exact repeat of verse 313, probably a copyist's doubling.
event: Soldiers go out to the beat of drums while the townspeople tremble.

reading: On the day when this elephant tears open travellers' chests and wrecks groves and pools, great ascetics come to the grove.
nuance: The verse sets the elephant's violence and the ascetics' arrival side by side without saying whether the one answers the other.
event: Great ascetics arrive in the grove on the day of the elephant's ravages.

reading: The ascetics who expound the four Vedas and make their deeds vanish come on a pilgrimage and settle in the grove.
nuance: The verse calls the four things they expound வேதம்; whether this means the Jain fourfold teaching or the Vedas is not stated and nothing here decides it.
event: Ascetics expound their four texts and settle in the grove.

reading: Charana ascetics who move over flowers, over waves and over fruit and leaves, and others who go over learned books, are listed.
nuance: The Charanas are ascetics with the power of going through the air; the listing is a catalogue of their powers and makes no claim.
event: Charana ascetics who travel over flowers, water and fruit are listed.

reading: Some Charanas go on mountain tops, in the sky, a finger above the ground, or a span above the ground, in the power of their vow.
nuance: The listing continues from verse 319 and keeps the same powers.
event: Charana ascetics go through the sky and above the ground by their power.

reading: Great sages hidden in mountain caves, freed of impurity, send down a rain of virtue that ends the world's distress.
nuance: அறமழை could be a literal rain given by ascetic power or the shower of teaching; the verse does not decide.
event: Sages in the caves send rain that relieves the world's distress.

reading: A great sage keeping a fortnight's fast comes at noon to take food from his palm, and the virtue of such worthy ones is hard to tell.
nuance: Food taken from the palm is a mark of strict ascetic practice; the verse praises by the discipline itself.
event: A sage on a fortnightly fast goes at noon to eat food from his palm.

reading: The leader of the Dharma-heroes speaks of the fearful bondage of suffering that is life, and all who have come hear his holy word with attention.
nuance: விலங்கும் may mean a fetter, binding, or the animals; the first sense fits the ascetic teaching, but the reading is not fixed.
event: The leader of the Dharma-heroes preaches and the gathered hear him.

reading: Hawks and other birds, drawn by the wish to feed, crowd the sky above and below and the kites go before and behind, for the elephant has left a feast.
nuance: The verse returns to the elephant's ravages after the ascetic verses, so the order of 317 to 324 may be disturbed.
event: Birds gather to feed on what the elephant has left.

title: துறவுக் காண்டம் 325-346 (2/3)
theme: The elephant, calmed by a sage's dharma, comes to Udayanan; the king hears the Jain teaching, learns the elephant was a brahmin ruined by lust and drink, and starts to hear of his own former birth as Gomukan.
source_issues: Verse 325 line 4: the form மறித்து is hard.
Verse 327 line 3: கோன கருன்னி is hard to read.
Verses 332 line 1 and 343 line 4 are hard to parse.
Verses 344 and 345: the names மாதவன், அயந்தன் and காமன் may name one person each or two; taken as one.
Verse 336 lines 3 and 4 are the sage's words in the narrator's frame.

cast.role: the king of Vatsa, who rides the elephant and hears the sage
Udayanan's minister who reads the elephant's calm
the sage who teaches dharma and tells the elephant's story
the elephant that listens to the sage and comes to the king
the gate guards and doorkeepers
the elephant keepers
the brahmin of Kadakam who in the sage's tale became the elephant
Vidapakan's wife
the noble wife who bears Gomukan
Udayanan's former self, born in Sugandhi
Gomukan's friend, son of the spear-king

reading: The elephant that had risen in a death-like rage hears the sage's dharma, bows its ears to it and understands its own unavoidable birth.
nuance: Line 4 turns on a hard form (மறித்து உணர்ந்தது); that the elephant knows its former birth is the likely sense, and verses 336 to 339 bear it out.
event: The enraged elephant is calmed by the sage's teaching and recalls its former birth.

reading: The sage teaches that the deed of killing, which makes blood run in streams, drives the killer to terrible sorrow, to animal births and then down into hard hell.
nuance: The verse is the sermon the elephant heard in 325; the sage speaks to the whole assembly and the elephant is the one who takes it in.

reading: With tears running and its mind pained, the elephant that had grown wise thinks of the king and comes to the gate of the city rampart.
nuance: Line 3 is hard (கோன கருன்னி); read here as the king's city and the elephant thinking of it.
event: The elephant weeps and goes to the rampart gate of the king's city.

tamil: கடையுடைக் காவ லாளர் கதவினைத் திறக்கப் போந்தே
நடுநகர் வீதி சென்று நரபதி மனையைச் சார்ந்து
நெடுவரை போல நின்ற நீர்மையை வாயி லாளர்
முடிமனற் குரைப்ப முன்னிப் பெருமக னெழுந்து வந்தான்.
reading: The gate guards open the doors, the elephant walks through the city to the palace and stands like a mountain, and the doorkeepers tell the king, who comes out.
event: The elephant reaches the palace gate; the doorkeepers report it and Udayanan comes out.

tamil: திருமுடி மன்ன னின்ற திருநிறை யானை கண்டு
மருவிய வமைச்சர் தம்மை மன்னவ னினிதி னோக்கப்
பெருவிரல் யூகி சொல்வான் பெருந்தவர் பால றத்தை
மருவியே கேட்ட தாகும் மன்னநீ யேற வென்றான்.
reading: Seeing the great elephant standing, the king looks kindly at his ministers, and Yugi says it has surely heard dharma from a great ascetic and bids the king mount it.
nuance: Yugi infers the sermon only from the elephant's bearing; the sage himself has not yet been named in this chapter.
event: Yugi reads the elephant's calm as the sign of a sage's teaching and urges Udayanan to ride it.

tamil: வேந்தனுங் கேட்டு வந்து வெண்கோட்டி னடிவைத் தேறிச்
சேந்தன னெருத்தின் மீதிற் றிரும்பிக்கொண் டேகி வேழம்
பூந்தளிர் நிறைந்தி லங்கும் பொழில்வலஞ் சுற்ற வந்து
காந்துநன் மணிப்பூண் மார்பன் கைம்மாவிட் டிழிந்தா னன்றே.
reading: The king mounts the elephant by its tusk, rides round the garden of fresh shoots, and gets down at the sage's place.
event: Udayanan rides the elephant round the grove and dismounts.

tamil: விரைகமழ் பூவு நீரும் வேண்டிய பலமு மேந்திப்
பரிசனஞ் சூழத் சென்று பார்த்திப னினிய னாகி
மருமலர் கொண்டு வாழ்த்தி மாதவ ரடியி றைஞ்ச
இருவென விருக்கை காட்ட விருந்துநல் லறத்தைக் கேட்டான்.
reading: The king takes flowers, water and fruit with his people, bows to the sage's feet in good humour, is told to sit and hears the dharma.
event: Udayanan honours the sage with offerings, sits at his bidding and listens to his teaching.

tamil: அறத்திற முனிவன் சொல்ல வரசனுங் கேட்க லுற்றான்
பெறற்கரு மருங்க லங்கள் பேணுதற் கரிய வாகும்
திறத்தறி பொருள்க ளாறுந் தேர்ந்துபஞ் சாத்தி காயம்
மறித்தறி தத்து வங்கள் வரிசையி னேழ தாமே.
reading: The sage begins his teaching: the six substances to be understood, the five that occupy space, and the seven truths, in order.
nuance: The six substances and the pancastikaya are the Jain categories; the verse only names them and does not define them.
event: The sage lays out the Jain categories of substances and truths.

tamil: சீரிய நவப தங்கள் செப்பிய காய மாறும்
வீரியப் பொறிக ளாறும் வேண்டிய வடக்க மாகும்
ஓரிய லறம்பத் தோடு மொருங்குபன் னிரண்டு சிந்தை
ஆரிய ரறிந்து நம்பி யதன்வழி யொழுக்க மாகும்.
reading: The sage goes on to nine categories, six bodily classes, restraint of the six powers, ten virtues and twelve contemplations, and says the noble know, believe, and then walk the way that follows.
nuance: Lines 1 to 3 are a list of Jain headings (navapadartha, the six kayas, ten dharmas, twelve anuprekshas); the verse gives names, not their sense.

tamil: தலைமகார் சிறப்புச் செய்து தன்மைநல் வாய்மை யான
கலையினற் கரையைக் கண்டு காதனூல் வழியைச் சென்று
மலைவில்சீர் மாத வர்க்கு வண்மையிற் றானஞ் செய்தார்
தொலைவிலாப் பிறவி நீங்கித் தொல்சுகக் கடலு ளாழ்வார்.
reading: Those who honour the great teachers, reach the end of true learning by the beloved books and give gifts to the ascetics are freed from endless birth and sink in the old sea of joy.
nuance: The reward is release; a gift here is a step on the road to freedom, not only a duty to the poor.

reading: As the sage teaches dharma the king bows again, and the sight of dharma is said to be the chief light that shakes off the stain of heavy deeds.
nuance: Here deeds are shed by sight and understanding, not by worship of a god.
event: The king bows after the sermon; the narrator names right vision as the means of shedding strong karma.

reading: The king asks the sage what is behind the elephant's rage, and the sage begins at a town of brahmins in the flower-grove country of Sali.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 are the sage's own words, set in the narrator's frame.
event: Udayanan asks the cause of the elephant's fury; the sage starts his answer.

reading: A brahmin of the village of Kadakam called Vidapakan lives with his wife Janaki in boundless desire.
event: Vidapakan and his wife live in endless passion.

reading: Vidapakan falls for the courtesan Amari, and in his longing neglects the rites and conduct of his religion and has no fear of sin.
nuance: The sage does not blame the courtesan; the fault is placed on the man's neglect of duty and absence of fear.
event: Vidapakan leaves his wife's side for the courtesan and drops his duties.

reading: Drunk with desire and with liquor, never letting go, a woman beside him, he knew neither night nor day, and after his death he became this elephant.
nuance: This is the sage's answer to the question of 336: the raging elephant is the brahmin who lived without restraint.
event: Vidapakan lives drunk and dies, and is reborn as the elephant.

reading: Hearing that the elephant has grown calm, the king tells the keepers to bathe it in pure water and feed it rice and milk-ghee with love.
nuance: Line 1 is said by the report-bearers; the order follows in the king's words.
event: Udayanan orders the elephant bathed and tenderly fed.

reading: The king orders daily feeding, bows his crowned head at the sage's feet, goes to him and asks him one more thing.
event: Udayanan orders the daily feed, bows, and puts a further question to the sage.

reading: The king asks what causes his own lasting love for the rutting elephant, and the sage says to hear it, for those of flawless sight and conduct hold no pride.
nuance: Lines 1 and 2 are the king's question and lines 3 and 4 the sage's reply; the speaker is given as the king.
event: Udayanan asks why he loves the elephant; the sage tells him to listen.

reading: The sage begins his account on the silver mountain's northern range, in the middle country with the lord's pond.
nuance: The place is Vijayardha's northern range (வெள்ளியம்மலை), a Vidyadhara country; line 4 is hard to place.
event: The sage begins the tale of Udayanan's former birth.

reading: In the city of Sugandhi, a lord of famed word and clear mind named Ayanthan has a noble wife who gladly bears him a son named Gomukan.
nuance: Whether மாதவன் and அயந்தன் name one man or two is not settled here; they are taken as one.
event: Gomukan is born in Sugandhi.

reading: The youth called Kaman, whose nurse is Somasundari, and Vijayan, son of the famed spear-king, become close friends.
nuance: Kaman is taken to be another name for Gomukan, since 346 goes on with Gomukan; this is not stated.
event: Gomukan and Vijayan become close friends.

reading: Gomukan enjoyed pleasures in love without limit, and when he died the good soul rose and you became.
nuance: The verse leaves the elephant's tie to Gomukan for the verses that follow; it only says the king was Gomukan.
event: The sage tells the king he was Gomukan in a former birth.

title: துறவுக் காண்டம் 347-367 (3/3)
theme: The sage explains the elephant's former birth and its seven days; after its death in samadhi the king crowns Gomukhan, takes initiation with his queens and ministers, and on a hill burns the two deeds and reaches perfection while the others are reborn as gods.
source_issues: Verses 347, 348, 350, 355 and 361 to 364 have corrupt or dense lines in the edition, so some sense is partly inferred.
Verse 365 has five lines; verse 359 has one line repaired in the edition (pulli after a vowel sign).
Whether the sage of 347 to 349 is the sage of 358 is not said, and whether the son called in 354 is Naravahanan is not said.

cast.role: the sage who explains the elephant's former birth and later teaches the king; 358 calls him அருண் முனிவர், and whether it is one sage is not said
the man whose former birth the elephant is
the Vatsa king, now ready to renounce
the king's messengers who bring news of the elephant
the elephant whose past life the sage tells
the son the king summons; whether he is Naravahanan of the earlier chapters is not said
the man crowned lord of the Vatsa land
the king's wives who choose to go with him
the king's minister and friend
the king's minister and friend
the ministers (Urumannuvan, Vidapakan, Yugi, Vayantakan) who take the vow

reading: The sage says the elephant was once Vijayan, who died deluded by lust and was reborn here as an elephant.
nuance: Lines 1 and 4 are corrupt in the edition: the words for the brahmin birth and for what the elephant eats do not parse cleanly, and the sense of இசையினால் (fame, music or sound) is open.
event: The sage explains that the elephant was Vijayan in a former life, reborn as a beast after dying in lustful delusion.

reading: The sages tell the king that his love for this elephant comes from an old tie to a friend, and that the elephant has seven days of life left.
nuance: The first line (மித்திரன் முன்பு வீறுநற காதலால்) is unclear; it is read as an old bond with a friend named Mitran, not as a claim about hell.
event: The sages tell the king the elephant's remaining span is seven days.

reading: Having listened to the sage's wise words, the king is grieved and goes to the elephant to speak to it in melting love.
event: The king, grieved by the sage's word, goes to the elephant and speaks to it.

reading: The elephant is bound with a cord, a sharp thorn is driven in and its legs are shackled, with the words that it should bear it.
nuance: Who binds the elephant is not said in the verse; it is read as the king's men acting for the king, who is addressing the elephant in the last line.
event: The elephant is tied, pricked with a thorn and shackled, and told to endure.

reading: The king strokes the beloved elephant, which bows low to him, and asks the keepers to tell the nature of such strong elephants.
event: The king touches the elephant, it bows, and he asks about the elephant's nature.

reading: The king tells the elephant-keepers what he wants, worships the sages' feet in love, and goes home with his army about him.
event: The king instructs the keepers, worships the sages and returns to his palace.

reading: Messengers come in the morning to report the elephant's good character and wellbeing; the king worships the Arugan in the temple, eats milk-rice with ghee and passes the days.
nuance: The elephant's fitness is said to include sheela, virtue, and plenty (சீலமும் வளங்களும்), the word used for conduct in Jain ethics.
event: Messengers bring news of the elephant, and the king worships in the temple before his meal.

reading: The elephant meets death in samadhi and is reborn a god in a good heaven; the king, hearing of it, sees that his kingdom and its pleasures will not last and calls his son.
nuance: Line 1 (சல்லகீணை, a lute) and the clause on the elephant 'doing its due' (முறை செய்ய) are unclear, so the order of the elephant's death and the god's rebirth is read loosely. The lute is the king's way of reaching the elephant in earlier verses, so it may only recall that.
event: The elephant dies in samadhi and becomes a god; the king, hearing this, resolves to give up his rule and summons his son.

reading: The son bows to his father's feet; the king tells him to live as lord of the earth, and he asks what use a matchless kingdom is to him.
nuance: The son's words in lines 3 and 4 are broken: they are read as a refusal of the rule for the sake of austerity, not as an acceptance.
event: The king offers the earth to his son, who refuses the matchless kingdom.

reading: The king crowns Gomukhan with the victor's jewelled crown as lord of the Vatsa land, tells him to rule the world well, then turns to his wives.
nuance: The crown goes to Gomukhan and not to the son called in 354; whether he is the son or a minister-friend of that name is not said here.
event: The king crowns Gomukhan king of the Vatsa land and addresses his queens.

reading: The king asks his wives to say what they wish, since he will leave the house for austerity; they answer that going is what they too want, and they will bear the faultless tapas with him.
event: The king announces that he will leave home for austerity, and his wives choose to go with him.

reading: The ministers Urumannuvan, Vidapakan, Yugi and Vayantakan, the king and the queens walk round the flowering grove and bow in love at the sage's feet.
nuance: The sage here (அருண் முனிவர்) is not named; he may be the sage of 347 to 349 or another.
event: The king, his queens and his four ministers go round the grove and bow at the sage's feet.

reading: The king praises the sage with hymns, listens in joy to the teaching of dharma, and asks the sage to give them the tapas worth praising.
event: The king hymns the sage, hears the dharma and asks for initiation.

reading: The sage, finding the time right, gives right view, knowledge and conduct; then they pull out their hair and take up austerity.
event: The sage instructs them and they take the vows, shedding their hair.

reading: They protect the six classes of living bodies with compassion, hold the senses in the mind, undertake the vows that give merit, and, knowing fasting to be hard, practise a faultless meditation that clears the mind.
nuance: Line 3 (அறிகுறி அநசனம் ஆற்றுதற்கு அரிது) is read as a remark that fasting is hard to keep; the wording is dense.

reading: Giving up the pull of enjoyment outside and within, they guard life with compassion, learn the regulated conduct and the restraint of thought, and enter meditation.
A numbered scheme of the ascetic's discipline: one kind of mind, two kinds of renunciation, three restraints, four instincts overcome, the five senses held, and further groups of six and seven.
nuance: Lines 3 and 4 (the six, the two kinds of nurse, the seven) are corrupt or use technical terms the Tamil alone does not explain, so only the first lines are read with confidence.

reading: The list continues in numbers, eight purities, nine, ten, eleven limbs, twelve, thirteen actions and fourteen, all of which they learn together.
nuance: The verse is a string of numbers whose terms the Tamil does not name (only 'purities', 'limbs' and 'actions' are plain); the numbered list is recorded, not decoded.

reading: The sage Udayanan on a great hill, with a glad heart, burns the two deeds in meditation, reaches perfection and sits in supreme bliss.
nuance: The verse has five lines in the edition.
event: Udayanan, now a sage, burns the two kinds of deed in meditation on a hill and attains perfection.

reading: The ministers and the queens, keeping the vow and dying in samadhi, are reborn as gods who enjoy bliss in heavens as their merit allows.
nuance: The ministers and queens are tied to a heaven in a level lower than the king's final state in 365: he reaches perfection, they a heaven of limited joy.
event: The ministers and the queens die in samadhi after their vow and are reborn as gods.

reading: The great ascetics, skilled in the way, enjoyed the bliss they wanted, which the verse sets beside the joys of embrace, touch, wonder and sweet words, thought rare to find.
