nuance: The poison she had prepared for the king is returned to her mouth.
event: The tormentors force poison on Amritamati, who burns without dying.

reading: They tell her that she did not shun the flesh her kin once gave, and now bid her eat her own limbs; they cut them off and call her glutton as she wanders in pain.
nuance: The reproach names flesh eaten from 'your kin' of an earlier birth, so the verse joins eating flesh with the earlier life's deeds.
event: The tormentors cut off Amritamati's limbs and make her eat them.

reading: They press her in a sesame mill, roast her on the fire of the furnace, set her on the killing stake and shake and crush her; the muni says the pain of the furnace cannot be told.
event: The tormentors mill, roast and impale Amritamati.

reading: The muni reckons that the smoke hell's torments, placed over ten and twenty-five and beyond, fall on her for ten and seven oceans of years.
nuance: The arithmetic of lines 1 to 3 is hard to resolve; line 4 gives the term as ten and seven oceans. Set against the ten oceans of Asokan's heaven in verse 285, the wife's term is longer.

reading: The muni says that Amritamati has not yet suffered all: an old deed stands and burns her in that hell, with other pains besides, and one tongue cannot tell them in one telling.
The muni turns to Yasodharan and his mother: through the cruelty of their earlier deed of taking life they fell into animal births and long trembling pain, and he begins to name them.
nuance: The verse names the cause as உயிர்க்கொலை வினைக்கொடுமை but not the act itself; the earlier chapters of the story supply it.
event: Yasodharan and his mother pass into animal births in return for killing.

reading: The muni says the former king became a peacock, a thorn-toothed beast, a fish and twice a goat, then a caged cock that took the vow, and now grows up as the king's own son Abhaya.
nuance: The first beasts are hard to name: மயிரி and முள்ளெயின are rare words. The speaker is told 'your son Abhaya', so the king addressed is the twins' father.
event: Yasodharan is named through his animal births up to birth as Abhaya.

reading: The muni says the mother took the forms of a dog, a snake, a crocodile, a goat, a buffalo and a cock, and when her old deeds loosened and she took the vow the muni taught, she grows as the king's daughter Abhayamati.
event: Chandramathi is named through her animal births up to birth as Abhayamati.

reading: As the muni tells that this is the fruit of his kin's deeds, the king weighs each point, his mind melts and he is bewildered.
nuance: Lines 1 to 3 are partly obscure in the edition; the king's state at line 4 is clear.
event: The king, hearing the muni's account of his kin's births, is bewildered.

reading: The king, having heard the muni, sends the man at his side to fetch Abhayaruchi and Abhayamati, and they come and bow at the feet of the gracious guru.
event: The king sends for the twins, who come and bow to the muni.

reading: Abhayaruchi and Abhayamati stand unable to bear it, and by a king's grace they remember and understand the births they had left behind; who else can tell what grief they bear.
nuance: Whose grace gives the memory (அரசன் அருளால்) is not clear: the king, or the muni spoken of as a lord of ascetics.
event: The twins recall their past births.

tamil: மக்களு ளிரட்டை யாக மாறினம் பிறந்த யாமுன்
மிக்கதீ வினையா லுற்ற விளைவினை யுணர்ந்தே மைய
துக்கமே தொடர நோற்றுத் துணையறந் துறந்த பெற்றி
இக்கதி துன்னிக் கண்டே மினிக்கதிக் கென்செய் வோமே.
reading: The twins say that, born as a pair among men, they have understood the fruit of their former evil deed, that they gave up the dharma that was their companion while enduring pain, and ask what they should do for the birth to come.
nuance: The twins speak together; the word ஐய addresses the muni.

tamil: தந்தையுந் தந்த தாயு மாகிய தழுவு காதல்
மைந்தனு மடந்தை தானு மாற்றிடைச் சுழன்ற பெற்றி
சிந்தையி னினைந்து நொந்து தேம்பினர் புலம்பக் கண்டு
கொந்தெரி யழலுள் வீழ்ந்த கொள்கைய னானான் மன்னன்.
reading: The father, the mother, the loved son and the daughter have turned in the stream of births; the twins brood on this and weep, and the king, seeing them lament, is as one fallen in blazing fire.
nuance: The relations named (father, mother, son, daughter) are those the earlier verses give to Yasodharan, Chandramathi and the king's children.
event: The twins weep over the kin they have been to one another, and the king is struck.

tamil: எந்தையும் எந்தை தாயும் எய்திய பிறவி தோறும்
வெந்துயர் விளைவு செய்த வினையினே னென்செய் கேனோ
அந்தமி லுயிர்கண் மாய வலைபல செய்து நாளும்
வெந்துயர் நரகின் வீழ்க்கும் வினைசெய்தே னென்செய் கேனோ.
reading: The king cries that in every birth his father and mother reached he gave them hard pain, that he has done deeds that cast life after life into hell, and asks what he is to do.

tamil: அருளொடு படர்தல் செய்யா தாருயிர்க் கழிவு செய்தே
பொருளொடு போக மேவிப் பொறியிலே னென்செய் கேனோ
அருளின துருவ மாய வடிகணும் மடிகட் கேயுந்
தெருளலன் நினைந்த தீமைச் சிறியனே னென்செய் கேனோ.
reading: The king laments that he took life with no mercy, followed wealth and pleasure, understood nothing even about those with a merciful form, and asks what he is to do.
nuance: The phrase அருளொடு படர்தல் செய்யாது, 'going forth without mercy', names the lack as mercy rather than ignorance.

tamil: மாவியல் வடிவு தன்னை வதைசெய்தார் வண்ண மீதேல்
ஆவினி யளிய னேதும் அஞ்சிலே னவதி யென்கொல்
காவல வருளு கென்னக் கலங்கின னரசன் வீழ
மாவல அஞ்ச லென்றம் மாதவ னுரைவ ளர்த்தான்.
reading: Saying that if those who killed a form of flour fare so, he too, who feared nothing, must have an end, the king begs protection and falls trembling; the great ascetic tells him to fear not and goes on with his teaching.
nuance: மாவியல் வடிவு, read as a form made of flour, recalls the offering of the dough figure; it is not said in these lines whose death it was.
event: The king falls trembling and begs protection, and the muni bids him not fear and continues.

title: ஐந்தாஞ் சருக்கம் 308-330 (3/3)
theme: The converted king and his companions renounce and he dies in the fast; the twin ascetics also die and are born as gods, and the poem closes by naming dharma, the giving up of anger, knowledge and the vow as what a person should do.
source_issues: Verses 321 and 322 were printed in 8 half-lines and joined into 4 lines by the build.
Verse 327 line 4 ends in a stray ligature and a misprinted word (சூழ்நதார்).
Verses 313 to 315, 319, 323 and 325 have unclear grammar or speaker; roles are read from sequence and flagged uncertain.

cast.role: the youth ascetic, brother of Abhayamati, the king's teacher; unnamed except at 325
the young woman, Abhayaruchi's sister
the king of Rajapuram who ordered the offering and is here converted; unnamed in this chapter
the chief of ascetics named at 318
the king's merchant friend and counsellor
the son who hands the kingdom to his brother, named at 314; perhaps not the twin of 325
the young wife of Abhayan, unnamed
one of the king's sons, who receives rule at 323

tamil: அறிவில ராய காலத் தறிவில செய்த எல்லாம்
நெறியினி லறிவ தூற நின்றனர் விலகி நிற்பர்
அறியலர் வினைக ளாலே யருநவை படுநர் கையாற்
சிறியநல் வதங்கள் செய்தே தீவினை யகல்வர் காணாய்
reading: The speaker tells the king that those who know the way keep away from the wrongs done in the age of ignorance, while the unknowing are bound by their deeds and yet shed evil by keeping small good vows.
nuance: The speaker is not named; he is read as the youth who has been teaching the king since verse 66, and the one addressed as 'you' (காணாய்) as the king. 'Small vows' (சிறிய நல் வதங்கள்) are the lay vows, set below the ascetic's great vows.

tamil: அருள்புரி மனத்த ராகி யாருயிர்க் கபய நல்கிப்
பொருள்கொலை களவு காமம் பொய்யிவை புறக்க ணித்திட்
டிருள்புரி வினைகள் சேரா திறைவன தறத்தை யெய்தின்
reading: With a merciful mind give safety to every dear life, put aside taking life, theft, lust, lying and possession, and dark deeds will not gather; reaching the Lord's dharma, what comes to confuse one but heaven's joy?
nuance: 'பொருள்' in line 2 is read as the fifth vow, hold on possessions; the verse lists five things given up.

tamil: என்றலு மடிகள் பாதத் தெழின்முடி மலர்கள் சிந்தக்
கன்றிய வினைகள் தீரக் கருணையி னுருகி நெஞ்சிற்
சென்றன னறிவு காட்சித் திருவறத் தொருவ னானான்
வென்றவர் சரண டைந்தார் விளைப்பது வென்றி யன்றோ.
reading: At this the king bows so that flowers fall from his crown at the sage's feet, his hard deeds loosen, his heart melts in pity and he becomes one with the holy dharma of knowledge and faith; the verse closes that those who take refuge with the victors reap victory.
nuance: அறிவு காட்சி (knowledge and faith) names two of the three jewels of the Jain path; the verse does not name the third.
event: The king bows at the youth's feet and takes up the Jain faith.

tamil: வெருள்செயும் வினைகள் தம்மை வெருவிய மனத்த னாகி
மருள்செயு முருவ மாட்சி மகனொடு மங்கை தன்னை
அருள்பெரு குவகை தன்னா லமைவில னளிய னும்மைத்
தெருளலன் முன்பு செய்த சிறுமைகள் பொறுக்க என்றான்.
reading: Frightened of his terrifying deeds, the king looks with great joy at the youth and the maiden, and says he did not know them and is pitiable, and asks them to forgive his earlier wrongs.
nuance: The verse speaks of 'smaller wrongs' (சிறுமைகள்) as the king's own account of ordering the offering; the verse does not itself name the offering.
event: The king asks the twin ascetics to forgive what he did to them earlier.

tamil: ஓருயிர்த் தோழ னாகி யுறுதிசூழ் வணிகன் றன்னை
ஆருயிர்க் கரண மாய அடிகளோ டைய நீயும்
நேரெனக் கிறைவ னாக நினைவலென் றினிய கூறிப்
பாரியற் பொறையை நெஞ்சிற் பரிந்தனன் மன்னன் மன்னோ.
reading: The king says to the merchant, his one-life friend and counsellor, that with the lord who is the refuge of dear lives he will think of him also as his equal master, and so speaking sweetly feels forbearance for the earth's burden.
nuance: Whether 'the lord' of line 2 is the youth or the teacher Sudattan is not fixed by the verse; the speaker is read as the king by the sequence.
event: The king addresses his merchant friend as an equal and takes up forbearance.

tamil: மணிமுடி மகனுக் கீந்த மன்னவன் தன்னோ டேனை
அணிமுடி யரசர் தாமு மவனுயிர்த் துணைவ னான
வணிகனு மற்று ளாரு மாதவத் திறையை வாழ்த்தித்
துணிவினர் துறந்து மூவார் தொழுதெழு முருவு கொண்டார்.
reading: The king gives his jewelled crown to his son; with him the other crowned kings, the merchant who was his life's companion and the rest praise the great ascetic and, resolved, renounce.
nuance: Line 4 says they took the form that 'the three' bow to; the sense of மூவார் is unfixed and read here as the ascetic's form. Compare Asokan's renunciation with kings at verse 84.
event: The king crowns his son and renounces with kings and the merchant.

tamil: தாதைதன் துறவு முற்றத் தானுடன் பட்ட தல்லால்
ஓதநீர் வட்டந் தன்னை யொருதுகள் போல வுள்ளத்
தாதரம் பண்ணல் செல்லா னபயனு மரசு தன்னைக்
காதலன் குமரன் தம்பி கைப்படுத் தனன்வி டுத்தான்.
reading: The son agrees to his father's renunciation but, holding the whole earth no more than a speck of dust, feels no attachment and gives the kingdom into the hands of his younger brother.
nuance: Abhayan here is read as the son crowned in verse 313, because the verse speaks of his father's renunciation; whether he is the same man as the Abhayan of verse 325 is not settled in the Tamil.
event: Abhayan, the king's son, hands the kingdom to his younger brother and leaves it.

tamil: மாதவன் மலர்ந்த சொல்லான் மைந்தனும் மங்கை யாய
பேதையம் பிணைய னாளும் பிறப்பினி துணர்ந்த பின்னர்
ஆதரம் பண்ணல் போகத் தஞ்சினர் நெஞ்சின் எஞ்சா
மாதவன் சரண மாக வனமது துன்னி னாரே.
reading: By the ascetic's words the son and his young wife understand the nature of birth, fear the attachment of pleasures and, taking the great ascetic as refuge, enter the forest.
nuance: The wife is not named; 'மங்கையாய பேதை' is the young woman, and the pair are read as Abhayan and his wife by the sequence from 314.
event: The son and his wife go to the forest to follow the ascetic.

tamil: வினைக்கும் வினைகள் தம்மால் விளைபயன் வெறுப்பு மேவித்
தனசர ணணைந்து ளார்க்குத் தவவர சருளத் தாழ்ந்து
வினையின விளைவு தம்மை வெருவின மடிகள் மெய்யே
சினவரன் சரண மூழ்கிச் செறிதவம் படர்து மென்றார்.
reading: Weary of the fruit that deeds beget from deeds, the new disciples bow to the one in whose refuge they stand, who offers the ascetic's sovereignty, and say they dread the ripening of deeds and, plunging into the Jina's feet, will undertake dense austerity.
nuance: Unlike the youth's earlier counsel at verse 33 that fear of what is due gains nothing, here fear of karma's ripening is what drives them to austerity.
event: The disciples ask to follow the Jina's way of austerity.

tamil: ஆற்றல தமையப் பெற்றா லருந்தவ மமர்ந்து செய்ம்மின்
சாற்றிய வகையின் மேன்மேற் சையமா சைய மத்திற்
கேற்றிநின் றின்மை தன்னை யிதுபொழு துய்ம்மி னென்றான்
ஆற்றலுக் கேற்ற வாற்றா லவ்வழி யொழுகு கின்றார்.
reading: The teacher says that if strength allows they should practise great austerity, taking up in turn vows of the stated kinds up to the fasting to death, and that they should be released now; and they follow that path each as their strength allows.
nuance: சையமா சையம் (line 2) is obscure; it is read as the named stages of the vow, ending in the fast. The reading is provisional.
event: The teacher sets graded austerities and they follow them each by their strength.

tamil: அருங்கல மும்மை தம்மா லதிசய முடைய நோன்மைப்
பெருங்கழு வொருங்கு சூழப் பெறற்கருங் கணங்கள் தம்மாற்
சுருங்கலில் சுதத்த னென்னுந் துறவினுக் கரச னின்னுட்
டருங்கடி கமழுஞ் சோலை யதுனுள்வந் தினிதி ருந்தான்.
reading: The ascetic Sudattan, great in austerity and honoured by many companies, comes with a great retinue into a fragrant garden of the city and sits there in peace.
nuance: Sudattan appears first at verse 23, when he settles in a garden before the offering. This verse is read as a return, but the Tamil could also be read as recalling that first coming.
event: Sudattan comes to the garden of the city and settles there.

tamil: அனசன மமர்ந்த சிந்தை யருந்தவ னிசோம திக்குத்
தனயர்கள் தம்மை நோக்கித் தரியலீர் சரிதை போமின்
எனவவ ரிறைஞ்சி மெல்ல விந்நக ரத்து வந்தார்
அனையவ ராக எம்மை யறிகமற் றரச என்றான்.
reading: The ascetic, in the fast, looks at the sons of Yasomati and bids them go on their alms-round since they cannot endure; they bow and come to this city, and the speaker asks the king to know him as one of them.
nuance: Line 4 turns the verse into the youth's own words to the king; the 'sons of Yasomati' are read as the twins, because the youth tells his births from verse 65 on, but the case ending is hard.
event: Sudattan sends the twins out on the alms round; they come to the city.

tamil: இனையது பிறவி மாலை யெமரது மெமது மெண்ணின்
இனையது வினைகள் பின்னா னிடர்செய்த முறைமை தானும்
இனையது வெகுளி காமத் தெய்திய வியல்பு நாடின்
இனையது பெருமை தானு மிறைவன தறத்த தென்றான்.
reading: Such is the garland of births, ours and theirs, he says, such the order in which deeds gave pain, such how anger and desire came to be, and such the greatness of the Lord's dharma.
nuance: The verse is a summary of the story told in the earlier chapters; the 'we' (எமரது, எமது) takes the twins together.

tamil: செய்த வெந்தியக் கொலையொரு துகள்தனிற் சென்றுறு பவந்தோறும்
எய்து மாயிடிற் றீர்ந்திடாக் கொலையிஃ திருநில முடிவேந்தே.
மையல் கொண்டிவண் மன்னுயி ரெனைப்பல வதைசெய வருபாவத்
தெய்தும் வெந்துய ரெப்படித் தென்றுனைந் திரங்குகின் றனமென்றான்.
reading: The deadly deed of killing a flour effigy of a cock, he says, did not end but followed them across birth after birth; how, then, must it be for those who kill living beings with a clouded mind, and so he feels pity for them.
nuance: இந்தியக் கொலை (line 1) is read as the killing of the flour cock on which the whole story turns; the sense of the first line is hard and the reading is provisional.

tamil: ஐய நின்னரு ளாலுயிர்க் கொலையினி லருவினை நரகத்தாழ்ந்
தெய்தும் வெந்துய ரெனைப்பல கோடிகோ டியினுறு பழிதீர்ந்தேன்
பொய்ய தன்றிது புரவல குமரநின் புகழ்மொழி புணையாக
மையின் மாதவத் தொருகட லாடுதல் வலித்தன னினியென்றான்.
reading: The king says that by the speaker's grace he has been freed from the fault of the killing that would have sunk him in hell's endless pain, calls the words true, and resolves to bathe in the ocean of great austerity with the words of praise as his raft.
nuance: The speaker is read as the king, replying to the youth of 320-321; line 2 calls the pain 'many crores', and the verse calls the youth ஐய and குமர.
event: The king vows to take up great austerity.

tamil: இன்சொன் மாதரு மிளங்கிளைச் சுற்றமும் எரித்திர ளெனவஞ்சிப்
பொன் செய் மாமுடிப் புதல்வருட் புட்பதந் தற்கிது பொறையென்றே
மின்செய் தாரவன் வெறுத்தன னரசியல் விடுத்தவ ருடன்போகி
முன்சொன் மாமலர்ப் பொழிலினுண் முனிவரற் றொழுதுநன் முனியானான்.
reading: Fearing his sweet-spoken wife and young kin as a heap of fire, the king gives the burden of rule to Pushpadanta among his sons, leaves with those who leave rule, and bowing to the sage in the flower garden he told of before becomes a good ascetic.
nuance: The verse is hard in grammar: that Pushpadanta is a son of the king and receives the rule is read from line 2 but is not certain. This verse may restate verses 313 to 315, which also describe a king's renunciation with kin.
event: The king gives rule to Pushpadanta and becomes an ascetic in the garden.

tamil: வெய்ய தீவினை வெருவுறு மாதவம் விதியினின் றுதிகொண்டான்
ஐய தாமதி சயமுற வடங்கின னுடம்பினை யீவணிட்டே
மையல் வானிடை யனசனர் குழாங்களில் வானவன் றானகித்
தொய்யின் மாமுலைச் சுரவரர் மகளிர்தம் தொகுதியின் மகிழ்வுற்றான்.
reading: He keeps the fierce-deed-fearing great austerity by the rule, and in a moment of great restraint lays down his body here, becomes a god among the fasting ones in the high heaven, and rejoices in the company of celestial women.
nuance: Heaven is the fruit here, not release; verse 329 says the same dharma leads on to release (சிவகதி) after the gods' state.
event: The king dies in the fast and is born a god in heaven.

tamil: அண்ண லாகிய வபயனுந் தங்கையு மாயுக மிகையின்மை
நண்ணி நாயக முனிவனி லறிந்தனர் நவின்றனர் குணமெல்லாங்
கண்ணி னார்தம துருவின துடலங்கள் கழிந்தன கழிபோகத்
தெண்ணின் வானுல கத்திரண் டாவதி னிமையவர் தாமானார்.
reading: Abhayan and his sister learn from the lord-ascetic that their life is not long, tell of his virtues, give up their bodies as they had sought, and become gods in the second heaven.
nuance: Whether this Abhayan is the twin or the prince of verse 314 is not settled in the Tamil; the pairing with his sister makes the twin more likely.
event: The twin ascetics die in the fast and are born as gods in the second heaven.

tamil: அம்பொன் மாமுடி யலர்கதிர்க் குண்டல மருமணி திகழாரம்
செம்பொன் மாமணி தோள்வளை கடகங்கள் செறிகழன் முதலாய
நம்பு நாளொளி நகுகதிர்க் கலங்களி னலம்பொலிந் தழகார்ந்த
வம்பு வானிடு தனுவென வடிவுடை வானவ ரானாரே.
reading: The two gods are adorned with crown, earrings, jewelled necklaces, armlets and bracelets, bright like the rainbow, and become fair in form.

tamil: வந்து வானவர் திசைதொறும் வணங்கினர் வாழ்த்தினர் மலர்மாரி
மந்த மாருதந் துந்துபி வளரிசை மலிந்தன மறுகெங்கும்
அந்தி லாடினர் பாடினர் விரும்பிய வரம்பைய ரருகெல்லாம்
reading: The gods come to every quarter, bow and bless them, flowers rain, a soft wind and the drum sound in every street and celestial women dance and sing, while goddesses come about them like arrows of Kama.
event: The gods and celestial women gather to honour the new gods.

tamil: மாசின் மாமணி மேனியின் வாசமோ ரோசனை மணநாறத்
தேசொ ரோசனை திளைத்திட முளைத்தெழு தினகர னனையார்கள்
ஆசி லெண்குண னவதியொ டமைந்தன ரலைகட லளவெல்லாம்
ஏசில் வானுல கிணையிலின் பத்தினி லிசைந்துட னியல்கின்றார்.
reading: Their bodies breathe a fragrance for a league and shine for a league like suns; they have the eight great qualities and sight to the sea's end, and live together in the unmatched joy of the heavenly world.
nuance: அவதி (line 3) is the limit of knowledge held by those born in heaven; here it is attached to the eight qualities and read as heavenly sight, but the line is obscure.

reading: The way of the holy dharma, the poet says, holds back the force of fearful deeds, gives birth in the gods' world and then joins one to the peerless release; see its flowering.
nuance: Here heaven is a stage and release (சிவகதி) the end; the word சிவ means auspicious and does not point to the god Siva in a Jain work.

reading: What is to be made? dharma. What is to be dropped? anger. What is to be looked on? knowledge. What is to be guarded? the vow.
nuance: The closing verse of the book.
